record.ROLE_TEXT:
**Job Title: Seed Plant Manager**

**Job Summary:** 
The Seed Plant Manager is responsible for overseeing daily operations of the seed processing facility, ensuring production efficiency, quality standards, and regulatory compliance are consistently met. This role manages plant staff, coordinates production schedules, maintains equipment, and ensures accurate documentation throughout all seed handling and processing activities. The Seed Plant Manager plays a key leadership role in driving continuous improvement and supporting the success of the farm’s overall seed production program.

**Minimum Requirements:**

* Farm production and seed processing experience required.
* Knowledge of operating and maintaining seed cleaning and processing equipment (e.g., seed cleaners, carters, indents, gravity tables, aspirators, airlifts, mixers, and scale house).
* Supervisory experience in a production or plant environment preferred.
* Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, Outlook).
* Strong knowledge of safety standards and quality control processes.
* Ability to work extended hours, including weekends, as production demands require.
* Ability to pass background check and drug screening.
* Valid Oregon Driver’s License (ODL); ability to obtain a farm endorsement.

**Attributes:**

* Excellent leadership and communication skills, both verbal and written.
* Bilingual in Spanish is a plus but not required.
* Strong organizational skills with attention to detail and accuracy in documentation.
* Dependable, punctual, and proactive in problem-solving.
* Team-oriented with ability to delegate tasks, train employees, and monitor performance.
* Ability to lift and/or move up to 70 pounds.
* Skilled in operating forklifts and other plant/farm equipment.

**Duties & Responsibilities:**

**General Management:**

* Direct, supervise, and coordinate daily plant operations, including seed cleaning, conditioning, treating, and packaging.
* Establish and enforce quality control measures to meet company standards and customer requirements.
* Ensure compliance with federal, state, and local laws, including workplace safety and environmental regulations.
* Develop and manage production schedules to meet deadlines and optimize workflow.
* Provide leadership, training, and ongoing support to plant staff, fostering a safe and efficient work environment.

**Plant Operations & Production:**

* Manage seed receiving, storage, conditioning, and distribution.
* Oversee and monitor equipment performance; coordinate routine maintenance and schedule repairs as needed.
* Supervise bagging, treating, and shipping operations to ensure accuracy and efficiency.
* Maintain precise records of inventory, processing steps, and production results.
* Implement continuous improvement strategies for plant efficiency, safety, and cost management.
* Collaborate with other departments and farm management to align plant operations with overall production goals.

Job Type: Full-time

Pay: $28.00 - $30.00 per hour

Benefits:

* 401(k) matching
* Dental insurance
* Health insurance
* Paid time off
* Vision insurance

Ability to Commute:

* Stanfield, OR (Required)

Ability to Relocate:

* Stanfield, OR: Relocate before starting work (Required)

Work Location: In person

**Company Overview**

DeConna Ice Cream is a leading distributor of ice cream products, serving customers throughout Florida and surrounding states. Our commitment to quality and customer satisfaction drives us to deliver the finest ice cream selections to our clients.

**Position Summary**

We are hiring a Plant Manager for our Tampa location. In this role, you will oversee daily operations, including three delivery routes, the freezer crew, an office assistant, facility upkeep, and vehicle maintenance.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Provide excellent customer service and support day-to-day branch operations.
* Place stock orders and help ensure inventory needs are met.
* Complete cross-training in delivery, pre-sales, freezer picking, warehouse operations, and office tasks.
* Use computer systems accurately and efficiently.

**Qualifications and Expectations**

* Strong multitasking, punctuality, attention to detail, and customer service skills.
* A clear Motor Vehicle Record.
* Flexibility with start times, which vary by business need and may be as early as 4:00 a.m. on some days.
* Compensation will be discussed at the time of hire.

**How to Apply**

Please apply on Indeed. We will review your resume and contact qualified applicants.

DeConna Ice Cream is a drug-free workplace. Applicants are subject to a background check, Motor Vehicle Record review, and pre-employment drug testing.

Job Type: Full-time

Pay: $42,000.00 - $52,000.00 per year

Benefits:

* 401(k)
* Dental insurance
* Employee discount
* Health insurance
* Life insurance
* Paid time off
* Vision insurance

* Required to Pass a Level II Background Screening for the JLA?

* Plant management: 1 year (Required)

* English (Required)

**We're Hiring: Director of Operations | Poolwerx**

Are you a strategic operational leader passionate about driving franchise success and organic sales growth? Poolwerx is looking for a dynamic Director of Operations to lead our field operations team, coach franchise partners, and champion operational excellence across our network.

**About the Role**

Reporting directly to the Chief Operating Officer, the Director of Operations develops and coordinates the efforts of the Operations team. You will deliver high-value support service spanning business coaching, leadership, salesmanship, and operational execution—all while fostering a positive brand and sales culture among our Franchise Partners.

**Key Responsibilities**

* **Drive Growth:** Deliver planned organic sales growth projections for franchise partners and regions while optimizing tracking, measurement, and reward systems.
* **Network Expansion:** Partner with franchise development to facilitate the introduction of new partners, stores, and acquisition opportunities.
* **Leadership & Team Management:** Manage and empower Field Operations, Franchise Business Coaches (FBCs), Onboarding Specialists, Technical Trainers, and Customer Experience Teams.
* **Technical & Field Excellence:** Lead Technical Trainers to ensure technicians master cleaning, maintenance, service, and repair standards; spend time in-field conducting site visits with partners.
* **Cross-Functional Collaboration:** Work closely with Commercial (B2B), Supply Chain, and Marketing teams to unlock local and regional growth opportunities.
* **Operational Alignment & Innovation:** Act as Operations Advisor for Innovation/Evolution programs to drive standard practices across the entire network.

**What We're Looking For**

* **Education:** Undergraduate degree in Business Administration or a related field.
* **Experience:** Extensive field or sales management experience in a franchise, multi-site, or retail environment (pool industry experience highly desired).
* **Financial Acumen:** Strong business acumen with proven ability to analyze and report on P&L and manage departmental budgets.
* **Tech Savvy:** Proficient with Google Workspace, MS Office, CRM systems, and modern business improvement platforms.
* **Communication & Mindset:** Strong, influential communicator with a proactive, resilient, and collaborative "can-do" attitude.

**How to Apply**

If you're ready to take your leadership career to the next level with a growing industry leader, submit your application today or reach out directly to learn more!

Pay: $140,000.00 - $150,000.00 per year

Benefits:

* 401(k) matching
* Dental insurance
* Flexible schedule
* Flexible spending account
* Health insurance
* Health savings account
* Life insurance
* Paid time off
* Retirement plan
* Vision insurance

The Director of Operations provides executive leadership across operations and business management, aligning day-to-day execution with strategic priorities. This role oversees financial and budget management, guides projects and organizational change, and advances process improvement to support effective, sustainable business performance.

**Responsibilities**

* Lead operations management and coordinate business activities.
* Set strategic direction and translate priorities into plans.
* Oversee financial management and budget planning.
* Guide project management from planning through delivery.
* Identify opportunities for process improvement and efficiency.
* Lead change management and support effective adoption.
* Your impact: Strong operational and financial oversight helps teams use resources effectively and deliver on business priorities.

**Qualifications**

* Demonstrated capability in operations and business management.
* Executive leadership skills and sound strategic judgment.
* Knowledge of financial management and budget oversight.
* Project management skills, including planning and coordination.

* Clear communication and change leadership skills.

**Job Overview**

The Director of Operations leads business operations and operations management, turning strategic plans into clear priorities and effective execution. You’ll guide executive-level teams, manage budgets and financial performance, and strengthen processes across the organization. This role calls for confident leadership, sound judgment, and a practical, data-driven approach to change and growth.

**Responsibilities**

* Lead operational excellence initiatives, process improvement, and operational analysis to improve business performance.
* Direct strategic planning, project management, and program management, aligning work with organizational priorities.
* Oversee executive-level budget management, financial management, budgeting, forecasting, and profit and loss analysis.
* Manage business development and business development management, identifying opportunities and coordinating execution.
* Lead change management, including large-scale organizational change, and communicate plans and progress clearly to executives. Your impact: Clear priorities and disciplined execution help teams deliver reliable operations and better serve customers.

**Qualifications**

* Demonstrated experience in operations management, business management, strategic management, and operational management.
* Experience in senior leadership, executive leadership, executive-level team management, management, and supervising experience.
* Strong budget management, financial management, forecasting, and profit and loss analysis skills.
* Proven ability to lead process improvement, project management, business development, and organizational change.
* Excellent verbal communication with executives and a record of data-driven decision making and strategic planning.

Pay: $45.00 - $95.00 per hour

Expected hours: 40.0 per week

Benefits:

* Dental insurance
* Flexible schedule
* Parental leave
* Retirement plan
* Tuition reimbursement

Work Location: Hybrid remote in North Chicago, IL 60064

record.ROLE_TEXT:
UniSea is looking for an experienced Rendering Plant Manager to lead and manage operations of UniSea’s fish rendering plant in Dutch Harbor, Alaska. The Rendering Plant Manager will be working at our Dutch Harbor, Alaska operations.

The Rendering Plant Manager is responsible for managing all elements of production of Fish Meal, Bone Meal, Fish Oil, and other by-products at UniSea’s Meal Plant to achieve continuous operations and maximum profitability. Maintain efficient operations of Main Sump operation in compliance with all State and Federal requirements.

**Essential Duties**

1) Organize and manage production staff and manage activities of the Meal Plant processing operation and maintain operational performance of equipment in the Main Sump. Coordinate production based on G1 and G2 operations.

2) Work with the Maintenance department in proposing and making design changes in processing facilities and equipment to maximize plant efficiency. Submit work orders to maintain proper repair of processing facility on repair or installation work that the Meal Plant does not perform.

3) Counsel and train employees according to UniSea policies and procedures. Coach and motivate employees to achieve maximum performance and maintain high morale. Evaluate employee performance and take necessary steps to assist employees in improving performance. Administer discipline to employees as appropriate, including terminations.

4) Recommend capital equipment needs, methods of improvement, and tools and materials to maintain and improve competitive production efficiency.

5) Maintain knowledge about internal and external influences affecting the future of the industry and company.

6) Review and assure the accuracy of scale reports, production reports, shipping tallies, inventories and quality control reports.

7) Coordinate with machinery manufacturers in updating current technology as appropriate.

8) Assist safety personnel and promote good safety and hygiene procedures throughout the plant.

9) Maintain open communication with the Quality Assurance department to ensure product specification, micro, and labeling requirements are maintained.

10) Perform other duties as directed.

**Position Requirements**

· High School or equivalent is required.

· Vocational education in a skilled trade like Electrical, Plumbing, HVAC, or Welding is preferred.

· Must have a minimum of 6 years of experience working in a rendering plant.

· Must have 2 years of experience in managing and supervising employees.

· Must have excellent leadership, communication and interpersonal skills.

· Must be able and willing to work in a rendering plant and supervise employees’ work performance in the plant.

· Working proficiency with Microsoft Outlook, Excel and Teams.

· Must be able to pass a post offer drug screen and criminal background check.

**This is a salaried exempt position located in Dutch Harbor, Alaska with a starting salary within the range of $96,754 - $116,122 per year.**

UniSea offers a rich benefits package including:

- Free company provided housing and utilities for employees in Dutch Harbor, Alaska.

- Free meals for employees in the company galley. Discounted meals are available for family members living in Alaska.

- Annual travel allowance benefit

- Relocation assistance

- Medical/Dental/Vision insurance available after 60-day eligibility period is satisfied

- A variety of different voluntary coverages are offered – including AFLAC policies and additional life insurance for self and family members

- Flexible Spending Account (FSA) and Dependent Care Accounts are available after 60-day eligibility period is satisfied

- 401(k) plan and additional 3% employer contribution – after 6-month eligibility period is satisfied. UniSea matches 100% of your contributions up to the first 5%, plus makes an additional 3% employer contribution.

- Employer paid life insurance

- Paid vacation, sick leave, and holidays

UniSea is an Equal Employment Oppor

Job Overview

The Operations Director will oversee the company's day to day operations and work closely with leadership to ensure that business objectives are being met. This role is responsible for managing operational performance, supporting department managers, improving internal processes, and making sure teams have the direction and resources they need to do their jobs effectively.

You will work across finance, sales, customer service, and project management to keep business activities organized and running smoothly. The right person understands how to manage people and resources, keep an eye on financial performance, and address operational problems before they affect the business.

Responsibilities

Oversee daily business operations and work with department managers to establish priorities, assign responsibilities, and maintain consistent performance across teams.

Monitor profit and loss performance, review operating expenses, and work with finance to manage budgets and improve financial results.

Use financial reports, operational data, and Microsoft Excel to evaluate performance, identify problems, and support day to day business decisions.

Manage operational projects and process improvement initiatives, looking for practical ways to reduce unnecessary costs, improve efficiency, and strengthen service delivery.

Work with sales, business development, and customer service teams to coordinate activities and ensure that operational priorities support the company's business goals.

Review existing procedures and introduce improvements where needed, including the use of lean management principles to improve workflow and resource utilization.

Manage and support department managers, provide clear direction, and follow up on operational responsibilities and performance.

Work with senior leadership on business planning, resource allocation, and decisions that affect the company's operations and long term development.

Address operational challenges, resolve internal coordination issues, and ensure that important projects and business activities stay on track.

Experience and Qualifications

Demonstrated experience in operations management, business management, or a related management position, with a strong record of supervising teams and overseeing daily business activities.

Experience managing department managers, coordinating multiple business functions, and maintaining accountability across an organization.

Strong understanding of financial management, profit and loss oversight, operating budgets, and financial performance analysis.

Ability to interpret financial reports, analyze operational data, and use Microsoft Excel to support business decisions.

Experience with strategic planning, project management, process improvement, and operational performance management.

Strong leadership and communication skills, with the ability to guide managers, develop employees, and address business challenges.

A practical understanding of sales operations, business development, and customer service.

Familiarity with lean management principles and continuous improvement practices is valuable.

Good organizational skills, sound business judgment, and the ability to manage competing priorities while keeping teams focused on results.

Pay: $158,200.00 - $222,200.00 per year

**Plant Manager – Manufacturing**

**The Opportunity**

We are seeking an experienced Plant Manager to lead an established, mid-size manufacturing operation in Holt, Michigan. This is an opportunity for a well-rounded manufacturing leader to take ownership of the facility's overall business performance, providing strategic direction and leadership while driving operational excellence, profitability, and continued growth.

Reporting to the VP of Operations, the Plant Manager will have full responsibility for the facility's operational and financial performance, including full P&L accountability. This individual will oversee all aspects of the business, lead and develop the management team, and ensure the facility consistently achieves its financial, operational, quality, safety, and customer objectives.

**What We're Looking For**

We are looking for a seasoned manufacturing leader who understands how to run a plant as a business. The ideal candidate brings a strong combination of operational expertise, financial acumen, and business leadership, with a proven ability to translate company objectives into measurable results.

This person will be comfortable leading through department managers, establishing accountability, making sound business decisions, and developing a culture of continuous improvement. Equally important is the ability to balance the bigger picture with an understanding of what is happening on the plant floor.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Assume full ownership and accountability for the facility's overall performance, including P&L, profitability, operating costs, and financial results.
* Develop and execute annual operating plans, budgets, and business strategies aligned with company objectives.
* Monitor financial and operational performance, analyze results, identify areas of opportunity, and implement corrective actions as needed.
* Provide leadership and oversight across all plant functions, including production, quality, maintenance, materials, shipping, and safety.
* Lead, mentor, and develop the management team, establishing clear expectations, accountability, and performance standards.
* Provide direction and oversight to the Production Manager and other functional leaders, ensuring alignment across departments and consistent execution of business objectives.
* Drive improvements in productivity, labor efficiency, throughput, quality, on-time delivery, and overall operating costs.
* Identify and implement cost-reduction initiatives, process improvements, and operational efficiencies that positively impact the bottom line.
* Maintain strong customer relationships, ensuring customer requirements are met and issues are addressed promptly and effectively.
* Oversee workforce planning, staffing, employee development, and organizational effectiveness.
* Ensure a safe working environment and maintain compliance with applicable safety regulations, quality standards, and other requirements.
* Direct capital planning and investment decisions, evaluating equipment, technology, and facility improvements to support business needs and long-term growth.
* Establish and monitor key performance indicators, using data and financial reporting to measure results and drive continuous improvement.
* Partner with senior leadership to communicate facility performance, address business challenges, and identify opportunities for growth and improvement.

**Qualifications**

* Progressive leadership experience in a manufacturing environment, with demonstrated success managing an entire plant or manufacturing operation.
* Previous full P&L responsibility, including budgeting, financial reporting, cost management, and profitability.
* Broad understanding of manufacturing operations, including production, quality, maintenance, materials management, and supporting functions.
* Proven ability to improve financial and operational performance through effective planning, execution, and accountability.
* Experience leading and developing

With over 30 yrs. in the Landscape Rock and Construction Materials Supplier industry, **MDI ROCK** continues to be the largest family owned Landscape Supply Company in Arizona. With locations in Phoenix, Prescott, Queen Creek, Dewey, and Ash Fork.

**MDI ROCK** is currently seeking a **PLANT MANAGER** for our Dewey Rock Quarry located in **DEWEY, AZ**.

The Plant Manager will oversee all daily operations of the plant from production and manufacturing to ensuring employees meet company standards for Safety, Quality, and efficiency.

**Responsibilities**

* Plan, organize, direct and run optimum day-to-day operations to exceed our customers’ expectations
* Increase production, assets capacity and flexibility while minimizing unnecessary costs and maintaining current quality standards
* Be responsible for production output, product quality and on-time shipping
* Allocate resources effectively and fully utilize assets to produce optimal results
* Implement strategies in alignment with strategic initiatives and provide a clear sense of direction and focus
* Monitor operations and trigger corrective actions
* Share a trusting relationship with workgroup and recruit, manage and develop plant staff
* Develop systems and processes that track and optimize productivity and standards, metrics and performance targets to ensure effective return on assets
* Operate loaders, rock trucks, excavators, and drilling equipment

**Skills**

* Proven work experience as a plant manager
* Working knowledge and understanding of MSHA regulations and possess a strong personal commitment to safety believing all incidents are preventable
* Understanding of aggregate processing and equipment
* Excellent verbal, written and interpersonal communication skills and capable of developing and maintaining good relationships with company and regulatory agency personnel
* Knowledge of ATF and ADEQ laws and requirements
* Ability to create accountability and to lead by example
* Strong team building, decision-making and people management skills

**Perks:**

* Medical, Dental, and Vision after 90 days
* 401k with Employer Match after 90 days
* PTO/PST

**MDI ROCK supports the Drug Free Workplace Act and therefore requires pre-employment drug screening on all newly hired employees. All offers of employment are contingent upon the receipt of satisfactory drug screening results**.

**MDI ROCK** participates in E-Verify.

* 401(k) matching

* Health insurance
* Life insurance
* Paid time off
* Vision insurance

**Plant Manager Role Description – Händorn**

**Role Purpose**

The Plant Manager is responsible for leading all plant operations at Händorn in a way that reflects and reinforces Händorn’s Core Values. This role ensures safety, quality, efficiency, profitability, and scalability while modeling **Learning-Led Excellence**, **Make it Easier for Someone Else**, **Thinking Together, Win to Together**, and being **Determined to Succeed**.

The Plant Manager serves as the operational backbone of the company and is expected to serve on the Leadership Team, translating company strategy into disciplined execution while building a strong culture of accountability, continuous improvement, and teamwork.

This role is critical to supporting Händorn’s growth objectives as production leadership transitions and capacity expands.

**Key Outcomes (What Success Looks Like)**

* Safe, efficient, and scalable plant operations grounded in continuous learning
* Consistent on-time delivery and high-quality output that makes work easier downstream
* Clearly defined processes, standards, and accountability that reduce friction
* Strong team engagement, collaboration, and succession planning
* Accurate financial, production, and operational reporting
* Continuous improvement in cost, throughput, quality, and team capability

**Core Responsibilities**

**1. Leadership, Culture & Core Values**

* Lead by example, consistently modeling Händorn’s core values in decisions and behaviors
* Maintain and develop the management team through coaching, feedback, and accountability
* Set and reinforce clear expectations so teams can succeed without confusion
* Foster a culture of curiosity, learning, and improvement—treating challenges as opportunities
* Encourage collaboration across departments, breaking down silos and aligning goals
* Resolve department conflicts constructively and respectfully
* Act as Chief Change Implementer, helping teams navigate change with clarity and confidence
* Build stability and trust through integrity, transparency, and follow-through

**2. Operations & Production Management**

* Oversee daily plant operations, production scheduling, and capacity planning
* Increase throughput while maintaining safety, quality, and team sustainability
* Monitor and act on measurables related to safety, quality, delivery, cost, and efficiency
* Ensure shop layout, workflow, and material organization support ease of execution
* Manage fabrication employees and shop leadership with clear priorities and support
* Oversee maintenance, machine integration, and equipment utilization
* Serve as the final operational checkpoint before work enters production, ensuring accuracy and readiness

**3. Quality, Safety & Compliance**

* Champion a safety-first mindset and enforce safety protocols and health standards
* Monitor quality control reporting and address issues promptly and thoroughly
* Build systems that prevent errors rather than relying on heroics
* Ensure internal controls, documentation, and regulatory compliance
* Proactively identify and manage operational risks to the company

**4. Financial & Business Management**

* Own plant-level financial awareness, including cost control and profitability drivers
* Lead budgeting, forecasting, and financial reporting in partnership with leadership
* Identify cost-reduction opportunities without sacrificing quality or safety
* Approve purchasing within established limits, ensuring thoughtful and timely decisions
* Manage vendor relationships and lead commodity-level cost negotiations
* Support capital investment decisions with clear ROI and long-term impact analysis

**5. Planning, Measurables & Continuous Improvement**

* Create, maintain, and continuously refine operational measurables and scorecards and measurables
* Monitor capacity, inventory levels, and material flow to reduce bottlenecks
* Standardize processes and documentation to make work easier for others
* Lead continuous improvement initiatives roo

**Overview**

The Operations Director will play a critical leadership role in the transformation and growth of Sterling Pharmaceutical Services. This individual must be a results-driven leader capable of accelerating operational excellence, strengthening organizational accountability, and improving financial performance while maintaining the highest standards of quality, compliance, and safety. The successful candidate will possess a strong sense of urgency, a hands-on leadership style, and a demonstrated track record of leading operational improvements, driving profitability, and delivering measurable results during periods of significant change and growth. The Operations Director will partner closely with executive leadership and regularly communicate progress, strategy, and performance metrics to key stakeholders, including ownership and the Board of Directors.

**Responsibilities**

* Lead operational and organizational initiatives to improve profitability, cash flow, productivity, and customer satisfaction.
* Develop and execute strategic plans that align operational performance with company financial objectives.
* Establish a culture of accountability, urgency, continuous improvement, and measurable results.
* Identify, prioritize, and implement operational efficiencies that reduce costs and improve margins.
* Drive cross-functional execution against key business objectives and recovery plans.
* Monitor and report operational metrics to executive leadership and the Board of Directors.
* Prepare and deliver presentations to executive leadership, Board members, lenders, investors, and external stakeholders.
* Partner closely with the CEO and COO to develop operational strategies and communicate progress against strategic initiatives.
* Lead change management efforts and effectively manage resistance during transformation initiatives.
* Ensure rapid decision-making and execution while maintaining compliance, quality, and safety standards.

**Requirements**

* B.S. in Engineering or Science discipline
* 10+ years of Operations Leadership experience. GMP aseptic manufacturing experience a plus.
* Demonstrated experience leading business transformation, operational turnarounds, restructurings, or significant performance improvement initiatives.
* Strong financial acumen with experience managing budgets, forecasting, cost reduction programs, EBITDA improvement, and working capital initiatives.
* Experience presenting to Boards of Directors, private equity firms, investors, lenders, or ownership groups.
* Track record of building high-performing teams and holding leaders accountable to performance metrics.
* Exceptional executive communication and presentation skills.

**Additional Information**

* Candidates must be legally authorized to work in the United States. Sterling Pharmaceutical Services does not sponsor employment visas now or in the future for this position.
* Relocation assistance is not available for this role. Candidates should reside within a reasonable commuting distance of the facility or be willing to relocate at their own expense.
* Sterling Pharmaceutical Services is conducting this search directly and is not engaging external recruiting or search firms for this position. We respectfully request that agencies and recruiters refrain from contacting us regarding candidate submissions.

Pay: $140,000.00 - $180,000.00 per year

Benefits:

* 401(k)
* 401(k) matching
* Dental insurance
* Employee assistance program
* Health insurance
* Health savings account
* Life insurance
* Paid time off
* Vision insurance

Work Location: In person

record.ROLE_TEXT:
**The Director of Operations/Master Orchestrator** we want on our Pro Roofers Dream Team is someone who thrives on turning all the moving parts into a well-oiled machine! You are a natural leader who sees the big picture without ever losing sight of the details. Where others see obstacles, you see solutions. Where others see disorganization, you see an opportunity to build a better system.

You get a genuine sense of satisfaction from watching a team operate at its best because you've put the right people, processes, and expectations in place. You love numbers because they tell a story, and you know how to use that story to make things better. You're not afraid to roll up your sleeves, tackle a problem head-on, or have the tough conversations that keep everyone moving forward.

You're organized without being rigid and driven without losing your good nature. You know how to bring out the best in people while holding them accountable for results. You're a builder of systems, a solver of problems, and a master of follow-through. Most importantly, you take genuine pride in creating an operation that runs smoothly, profitably, and with excellence.

Job Duties/Responsibilities

* Be the driving force behind the day-to-day operations of Pro Roofers, ensuring everything runs efficiently from signed contract to completed project and final payment.
* Lead, support, and hold production teams accountable for completing jobs on time, within budget, and to our high standards of quality.
* Masterfully coordinate scheduling, material ordering, production, quality control, and billing to keep every job moving forward.
* Develop and maintain quality control processes that ensure exceptional workmanship and customer satisfaction.
* Keep a watchful eye on the production pipeline, anticipating problems and removing bottlenecks before they become costly.
* Track job costs, profit margins, and operational performance. You know your numbers and use them to make smart decisions!
* Create and monitor key performance indicators (KPIs) that keep the team focused on measurable results.
* Keep our CRM accurate, organized, and functioning as a valuable management tool.
* Lead productive team meetings and individual check-ins that create clarity, accountability, and momentum.
* Build, document, and continually improve systems that make our operations more efficient and scalable.
* Embrace technology, software, and AI tools to simplify processes and help our team work smarter.
* Partner with our sales leadership to ensure a seamless transition from the sale to successful project completion.
* Cultivate a team environment built on trust, excellence, personal responsibility, and a shared commitment to success.

Qualifications

* Proven experience managing operations in the roofing or solar industry.
* A natural ability to lead people, build strong relationships, and inspire accountability.
* Exceptional organizational skills with an almost instinctive ability to identify what needs attention.
* A strong understanding of job costing, profit margins, budgets, and operational performance metrics.
* A numbers-driven mindset. You appreciate accurate data and know how to turn it into actionable improvements.
* Experience implementing and improving operational systems and procedures.
* Confidence working with CRM systems and business management software.
* An appreciation for emerging technology, including AI, and its ability to improve business efficiency.
* Strong communication skills and the ability to navigate challenging conversations with professionalism.
* A commitment to quality, consistency, and doing things right the first time.
* A proactive, solution-oriented attitude. You don't wait for someone else to fix a problem. You take ownership and get it done!
* Willingness to work long hours during the busy season.
* Agility to climb on a roof and walk the ridge.

record.ROLE_TEXT:
**Job Overview**

Flexim Group is seeking an experienced Global Account Operations Manager to provide senior operational leadership for a strategic international account operating across complex sites and manufacturing environments.

Based in Jersey City, you will hold global accountability for operational performance across the account, leading regional and site teams to deliver consistent FM and technical services, safety, compliance and business continuity.

This is a management operations role requiring strong experience, technical credibility and the ability to lead through senior regional and site operations teams. You will set operational standards, challenge performance, manage critical escalations and translate global client priorities into disciplined execution across countries and facilities.

**Duties**

* Lead global operational performance across a complex, multi-country manufacturing account.
* Lead and challenge regional and site Operations Managers, ensuring clear accountability and consistent execution.
* Drive services excellence, with a strong focus on asset reliability, maintenance, utilities and critical infrastructure.
* Establish and enforce global operational standards, while ensuring effective implementation at regional and site level.
* Monitor and challenge operational performance through KPIs, SLAs, CMMS/BMS data, maintenance completion, backlog and asset uptime.
* Lead critical operational escalations.
* Drive continuous improvement and operational excellence, identifying opportunities to improve reliability, efficiency, service quality and cost performance.
* Lead global account financial performance, including budgeting, forecasting, cost control and profitability.
* Partner with senior client stakeholders, translating strategic objectives into operational priorities and measurable results.
* Act as the senior operational authority for the account, providing executive-level governance, reporting and decision-making.

**Experience**

* Substantial operational leadership experience in Integrated Facilities Management, ideally across a multi-country portfolio.
* Strong working knowledge of hard FM and building engineering services
* Demonstrated experience controlling SLAs, KPIs, CMMS workflows, asset registers, maintenance backlogs and technical compliance.
* Proven ownership of account P&L, budgeting, forecasting, subcontractor costs and commercial change control.
* Experience leading dispersed operational teams and managing specialist service providers across different regulatory environments.
* Confident client-facing leadership, supported by operational discipline, sound judgement and a willingness to be present on site.
* Significant leadership experience within Integrated Facilities Management.
* Proven success managing complex global or multi-country client accounts.
* Strong executive stakeholder management and relationship-building skills.
* Strong understanding of operational excellence, governance and performance management.
* Excellent communication, negotiation and influencing skills.
* A proactive, accountable and client-centric leadership style.

Pay: $135,000.00 - $150,000.00 per year

Benefits:

* 401(k)
* Dental insurance
* Flexible schedule
* Health insurance
* Paid time off
* Professional development assistance
* Retirement plan
* Vision insurance

Work Location: Hybrid remote in Jersey City, NJ 07307

record.ROLE_TEXT:
Coordinated Services Management (CSM) is an established senior living management company serving nonprofit and mission-driven organizations throughout Virginia. We are seeking an experienced Regional Director of Operations to provide leadership, guidance, and operational oversight for assigned skilled nursing, assisted living and memory care communities in Virginia. This position is based in Roanoke and requires regular travel to assigned communities.

The ideal candidate is a collaborative, results-oriented leader with strong operational and financial management skills, sound clinical knowledge, and a commitment to quality resident care and services.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Provide leadership, coaching, and operational oversight to community Executive Directors and leadership teams.
* Drive operational excellence, regulatory compliance, quality of care, resident satisfaction, and financial performance.
* Monitor occupancy, marketing effectiveness, staffing, budgets, and financial results, identifying opportunities for improvement and growth.
* Partner with community leadership and home office team to address operational challenges and implement effective solutions.
* Support leadership development, performance management, and succession planning.
* Guide strategic planning, capital improvements, and effective stewardship of community resources.

record.ROLE_TEXT:
Shield AI is a venture-backed defense-tech company with the mission of protecting service members and civilians with intelligent systems. Its products include Hivemind autonomy software, V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft, and Aechelon simulation and synthetic reality technologies. With offices and facilities across the U.S., Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific, Shield AI’s technology actively supports operations worldwide. For more information, visit www.shield.ai. Follow Shield AI on LinkedIn, X, Instagram, and YouTube.

### **Job Description:**

Shield AI is actively seeking candidates with deep expertise in manufacturing and quality methodologies, paired with a relentless drive to enable supplier success and strengthen mission-critical operations.

Shield AI’s Supply Chain Quality team is responsible for global quality oversight across our supplier base. The team reduces supply-chain risk through supplier assessments and internal risk reviews, proactively drives supplier qualification and development activities.

In this role, you will lead a supplier quality team responsible for supplier qualification, development, performance management, and quality assurance across Shield AI’s aerospace and defense supply base. You will set supplier-quality priorities; manage team capacity, technical execution, and resource allocation; and develop high-performing quality leaders. The role also oversees supplier audits, nonconformance resolution, root-cause investigations, and hands on hardware dispositions.

You will evaluate supplier capability, quality performance, organizational risk, and resource needs to ensure purchased hardware and materials meet Shield AI engineering, customer, regulatory, and quality requirements. As an experienced aerospace quality leader, you will partner closely with Supply Chain, Engineering, Manufacturing, Operations, and Program teams to resolve complex supplier-quality issues, improve supplier capability, and reduce quality and delivery risk across the supply base.

**What you'll do:**

* Develop the supplier quality team responsible for supplier qualification, surveillance, performance management, and corrective-action activities across Shield AI’s global aerospace and defense supply base.
* Establish supplier-quality priorities, allocate resources, and translate functional objectives into staffing, workload, and execution plans that support product, program, and organizational needs.
* Develop Supplier Quality leaders and engineering personnel through coaching, performance management, succession planning, workforce development, and technical mentorship.
* Oversee supplier qualification, risk assessments, periodic performance reviews, supplier audits, source inspections, and approved-supplier status across complex aerospace hardware, commodities, and manufacturing processes.
* Ensure supplier requirements are effectively flowed down and that suppliers comply with applicable quality management system, engineering, customer, contractual, regulatory, and statutory requirements.
* Escalate significant supplier-quality risks and direct SCARs, supplier recovery efforts, and capability-improvement plans that could affect product quality, delivery, mission readiness, or program execution.
* Partner with Engineering, Manufacturing, Operations, Supply Chain, and Program teams to address supplier producibility, design-for-manufacturability, process capability, technical execution, and quality risks.
* Advance supplier-quality processes, business systems, data analytics, and continuous-improvement practices that strengthen supplier capability, product quality, delivery performance, and supply-base resilience.

**Required qualifications:**

* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Quality, Manufacturing, or another related technical discipline.
* At least 7 years of relevant experience, including 2–5 years of leadership or people-management experience with direct responsibility for Quality Engineering and/or Supplier Quality

Job Summary - Why you’ll love this position

Are you motivated by the challenge of solving complex, enterprise-wide problems? Do you love asking "why" and transforming good operations into exceptional public experiences? If so, consider joining the State of Missouri as our next Director of Operational Excellence!

In this pivotal leadership role you will champion continuous improvement across state government, lead our operational initiatives, and oversee our statewide customer experience program. This position resides within the Office of Administration, the administrative arm of the executive branch, but leads efforts that span all executive agencies to improve service delivery to the citizens of Missouri.

We are seeking an energetic, visionary executive to lead and empower a dedicated team of process improvement and customer experience efforts while serving as a strategic partner to executive leadership, agency partners, and frontline public servants. Our next director is a bridge-builder who combines proven improvement methodologies with human-centered design, modern customer experience principles, rapid responsiveness to agency partner needs, and a passion for coaching state team members to achieve measurable public outcomes.

In addition to the inspiring work that will improve the services provided by state government and your colleagues work environment, you will receive a great benefits package that includes paid time off, medical/vision/dental insurance, life insurance, and retirement.

*The salary indicated represents a base pay rate. If the individual selected or the position is eligible for a pay differential (e.g., shift, security, or years of service), it will be added to the total compensation in your paycheck. A pay differential does not raise your base pay.*

Responsibilities - What you’ll do

* Work collaboratively with leadership and teams to encourage, develop, and execute strategies to create a culture of continuous improvement across Missouri state government. Measure the effectiveness of improvements and provide administration with visibility to such improvements.
* Act as a subject matter expert and promote change management by sharing Lean Six Sigma and other Operational Excellence best practices. Teach, mentor, coach and lead Operational Excellence leaders from every state department.
* Continuously provide helpful operational excellence resources for team members and facilitate training sessions.
* Model excellence in leadership and act with urgency to achieve results and lead efforts to cultivate a culture of data-based decision making.
* Facilitate, lead, and oversee state level strategic initiatives and other projects as assigned by leadership.
* Coordinate and host an annual Show Me Excellence Summit and represent the State of Missouri at national operational excellence events.

Qualifications - All you need for success

**Minimum Qualifications**

* A bachelor’s degree or equivalent
* Formal training in Lean Six Sigma or an equivalent continuous process improvement framework. Lean Six Sigma Green Belt or Black Belt certification is strongly preferred
* Demonstrated advanced knowledge in Lean and Operational Excellence frameworks and facilitation methodologies
* Hands-on experience work with survey, feedback, or data visualization platforms, such as Qualtrics, Tableau, or Power BI

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Must be action oriented, demonstrate superior organizational abilities and have strong facilitation skills and excellent communications skills.
* Ability to work with leaders and multi-level teams to establish goals, performance indicators, actions plans and deliverables and effectively communicating across broad audiences.
* Must have excellent leadership abilities. This individual must be an effective collaborator with energy, enthusiasm and a can-do attitude who can empower others, gain buy-in and achieve results.
* Good understanding of data analysis related to process improvement a

Shield AI is a venture-backed defense-tech company with the mission of protecting service members and civilians with intelligent systems. Its products include Hivemind autonomy software, V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft, and Aechelon simulation and synthetic reality technologies. With offices and facilities across the U.S., Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific, Shield AI’s technology actively supports operations worldwide. For more information, visit www.shield.ai https://shield.ai/. Follow Shield AI on LinkedIn https://www.linkedin.com/company/shield-ai, X https://x.com/shieldaitech, Instagram https://www.instagram.com/shield_ai, and YouTube https://www.youtube.com/@Shield_AI. 

 

Job Description:

The Senior Air Vehicle Operator (AVO) – Deployment Operations is responsible for executing and leading V-BAT flight operations in support of DoD and foreign customers in both land-based and maritime OCONUS environments. This is an operationally focused role requiring strong aviation judgment, disciplined execution, and the ability to lead small teams in austere and high-visibility conditions. 

 

The Senior AVO is responsible for leading mission planning activities, performing comprehensive risk assessments, delivering pre-mission briefings, executing flight operations, and conducting structured post-flight debriefs. This role includes conducting Functional Check Flights (FCFs) and system validation as required, ensuring aircraft configuration control and logbook accuracy, coordinating with maintenance to sustain fleet readiness, and supporting overall operational discipline. The Senior AVO will mentor junior operators, serve as the on-site operational representative to customers, and travel extensively in support of deployments. 

 

This is not an entry-level flight operations role. The ideal candidate brings strong aviation fundamentals, disciplined cockpit habits, and mature operational decision-making. They must be comfortable leading deployments, briefing customers, managing risk in dynamic environments, and maintaining professionalism in high-visibility settings. The Senior AVO must balance mission execution with customer satisfaction while upholding the highest standards of safety, compliance, and operational excellence. 

Required Qualifications:

 - Minimum of 2000 documented unmanned flight hours or 1000 manned flight hours 

 - Demonstrated instructor experience (manned or unmanned aviation)  

 - FAA Private Pilot License (PPL)  

 - FAA Part 107 Remote Pilot Certificate 

 - Ability to obtain and maintain an FAA Class II Medical Certificate 

 - Ability to obtain and hold a Secret DoD security clearance 

 - Ability to pass background, drug screening, and customer-required medical/dental screenings 

 - Willingness to travel up to 50–75% in support of deployments 

 - Ability to lead and operate independently in small teams under austere conditions 

 - Strong aviation judgment, decision-making, and risk management skills 

Preferred Qualifications

 - FAA Instrument Rating and/or Commercial Pilot License  

 - Experience operating as aircrew on manned aircraft  

 - Prior military service, particularly with overseas or deployed operations  

 - Maritime or shipboard UAS operational experience  

 - Previous experience as a Site Lead or in a leadership role overseeing aviation operations   

#LI-JM1

#LD

 

Full-time regular employee offer package:

Pay within range listed + Bonus + Benefits + Equity

 

Temporary employee offer package:

Pay within range listed above + temporary benefits package (applicable after 60 days of employment)

 

Salary compensation is influenced by a wide array of factors including but not limited to skill set, level of experience, licenses and certifications, and specific work location. All offers are contingent on a cleared background and possible reference check. Military fellows and part-time employees are not eligible for benefits. About Us

 

Skydweller Aero Inc. is a transatlantic, cutting-edge aerospace company developing solar-powered aircraft solutions capable of perpetual flight while carrying heavy and powerful payloads. Building on technology from the longest continuous renewably powered flight program in history, this fast-growing company is creating a new class of unmanned aircraft. It combines the persistence of geosynchronous satellites with the sensing capabilities and flexibility of a large airborne platform. Skydweller Aero Inc. has its global and US headquarters in Oklahoma City, with European operations headquartered in Spain.

Role Summary

 

As Skydweller prepares to move from development toward aircraft production, we are looking for an experienced manufacturing executive to build and lead our production organization. This role is based in **Oklahoma City, OK** and reports to the Chief Operating Officer.

The Vice President, Manufacturing & Production will own all aircraft production operations: final assembly, systems integration, avionics installation, production testing, factory operations and aircraft delivery. You will lead the organization as we scale from prototype and low-rate initial production into sustained manufacturing.

We are looking for a hands-on aerospace manufacturing leader with a proven track record of building production organizations, improving factory performance and delivering complex aircraft in FAA-regulated environments.

**Why join:** Most manufacturing leadership roles optimize an existing production system. This one builds it. You will establish the manufacturing organization, develop the factory workforce, and scale production of one of the most ambitious autonomous aircraft programs in aerospace.

Responsibilities

 

**Production leadership**

 

* Lead all aircraft production and manufacturing operations.
* Drive safe, efficient and repeatable aircraft production.
* Build and lead a high-performing manufacturing organization, with clear management systems, metrics and operating rhythms.
* Foster a culture of accountability, safety, quality and continuous improvement.

 

**Assembly and integration**

* Oversee final assembly, systems and electrical integration, avionics installation and aircraft completion.
* Ensure aircraft are built to engineering, quality and regulatory requirements.
* Drive production readiness and resolve manufacturing constraints and bottlenecks.

 

**Production planning and execution**

* Own execution of the Master Production Schedule.
* Lead production planning, labor allocation and resource management.
* Set capacity plans that support production-rate growth.
* Monitor factory performance and drive throughput, productivity and efficiency improvements.

 

**Production testing and acceptance**

* Lead production acceptance testing and ground test operations.
* Coordinate production readiness with Engineering, Quality, Flight Operations and Program Management.
* Ensure aircraft move smoothly from production through acceptance and delivery.

 

**Regulatory compliance and quality**

* Ensure compliance with FAA Part 21 production requirements and the company quality management system.
* Maintain production configuration control and manufacturing documentation discipline.
* Support internal, regulatory and customer audits and certification activities.
* Partner with Quality leadership to improve first-pass yield.

 

**Growth and scale-up**

* Develop the manufacturing infrastructure, facilities and staffing plans needed for higher production rates.
* Implement lean manufacturing and operational excellence initiatives.

 

**People leadership**

* Recruit, develop and mentor production leaders and technical staff.
* Establish workforce development and skills-training programs.
* Build strong partnerships across Engineering, Supply Chain, Quality, Flight Operations and Program Management.

 

Success Measures

You will be measured on aircraft delivery performance, production

**Description**

 
 
 
 

Title: Sr. Manager, Quality SME (BESS) 
Department: EHSQ / Quality 
Location: Houston, TX

Supervisor: Sr. Director of Quality 
Direct Reports: None 
FLSA Status: Exempt 
Position Status: Permanent, Full-time

Work Status (Remote/Hybrid/In-Office): Remote

Sr. Manager, Quality SME (BESS)

Hanwha Qcells USA Corp (“HQC US”) develops, invests, and delivers solar photovoltaic (PV) and battery energy storage systems (BESS) projects through Engineering, Procurement, Construction (EPC) services in North America.

The company brings a decade of global leadership in solar PV to deliver utility-scale power generation plants customized for local and regional energy markets. HQC US offers the full spectrum of PV solutions – from the core technology of cells and modules to large-scale project development and investment. With proven capabilities across the solar and battery storage chain, HQC US minimizes uncertainty and risk, and helps customers achieve a higher return on their investment in renewable energy.

SUMMARY

The Sr. Manager, Quality SME (BESS) (“Quality SME”) serves as the company’s subject matter expert and technical authority for Quality on Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) construction. The Quality SME is responsible for developing and maintaining the processes, systems, Inspection & Test Plan (ITP) templates, Quality Control Verification Checklists, and Standard Work Instructions (SWIs) that govern how Quality is planned, executed, and documented on BESS scopes, whether self-performed or subcontracted. The role covers both standalone BESS facilities and BESS integrated with utility-scale solar PV projects.

The Quality SME works alongside the Regional Quality Managers on every project with active BESS construction, integrating discipline requirements into the project Quality program and providing technical direction to the Quality Field Leads and Quality Inspectors hired for these scopes. Those personnel report to the assigned Site Quality Manager or Sr. Site Quality Manager, who remains the single point of contact and the ranking Quality authority on site. The Quality SME holds a matrixed line of technical direction to the discipline team, participates in hiring, onboarding, training, and performance input, and is accountable for the technical consistency, process discipline, and record integrity of BESS Quality across the portfolio.

Success in this role requires deep practical knowledge of utility-scale BESS construction, including equipment foundations and anchorage, battery enclosures and containers, power conversion systems (PCS) and inverters, medium-voltage transformers, auxiliary power, DC and AC cabling and terminations, grounding and bonding, thermal management systems, and fire detection, suppression, gas detection, and explosion control installation interfaces. Equally important is a working command of manufacturer-specific installation, preservation, and warranty requirements, which often govern acceptance more directly than the project drawings. The Quality SME aligns closely with the Engineering and BESS teams to integrate Quality early and resolve technical questions consistently. Design interpretation, battery management and energy management system configuration, functional commissioning, and capacity testing remain with Engineering, Commissioning, and the manufacturer; the Quality SME ensures those interfaces are defined, documented, and respected.

This position reports directly to the Senior Director of Quality (or another designated member of senior management). The role is remote, with standard business hours of Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. local time, or as site construction hours dictate during jobsite visits. Travel is required up to 50% of the time, which includes scheduled jobsite visits for oversight and technical authority, as well as short-notice trips and extended site visits as business needs dictate.

Plant Manager

**Piedmont, South Carolina | Industrial Adhesives**

Position Summary

We are seeking an experienced and dynamic **Plant Manager** to lead our manufacturing operation in **Piedmont, South Carolina**. This is a highly visible leadership role for a proven manufacturing leader who can **drive change, develop high-performing teams, strengthen accountability, and deliver operational excellence**.

The ideal candidate is a hands-on, people-focused leader who can set a clear vision, engage employees at all levels, challenge the status quo, and build a culture centered on **safety, quality, continuous improvement, collaboration, and results**.

Key Responsibilities

* Provide overall leadership and direction for plant operations, including **Safety, Quality, Delivery, Cost, People, and Continuous Improvement**.
* Lead **organizational and cultural change**, building employee engagement, accountability, and ownership.
* Develop, coach, and strengthen the plant leadership team while building the organization's future talent pipeline.
* Champion a zero-incident safety culture and ensure compliance with EHS requirements.
* Drive operational excellence using **Lean Six Sigma, OEE, VSM, root-cause analysis, and continuous improvement tools**.
* Deliver plant financial, productivity, quality, customer service, and inventory objectives.
* Partner across Operations, Supply Chain, Engineering, Quality, R&D, Sales, and other business functions to achieve business goals.
* Identify and eliminate barriers, improve processes, and create sustainable improvements in plant performance.
* Maintain a strong presence on the manufacturing floor and actively engage with supervisors and employees.
* Lead and support capital investments and improvement initiatives aligned with business strategy.

What We're Looking For

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Manufacturing, Operations, or a related technical discipline.
* 10+ years of progressive manufacturing, engineering, or operations experience.
* Proven manufacturing leadership experience with a strong record of **leading change and improving performance**.
* Demonstrated ability to **build, coach, and lead high-performing teams**.
* Strong business acumen with the ability to drive accountability and results.
* Experience with Lean Six Sigma and continuous improvement methodologies.
* Excellent communication, problem-solving, and decision-making skills.
* Chemical, specialty chemical, adhesives, batch/process manufacturing, or similar experience preferred.

The Leader We're Looking For

You are a **visible, decisive, and engaging leader** who knows how to bring people along through change. You set clear expectations, hold yourself and others accountable, develop talent, and create an environment where employees are empowered to solve problems and improve the business.

Most importantly, you can **deliver today's results while transforming the organization for tomorrow**.

Overview:

The Director of Operations is responsible for overseeing and coordinating operations across all markets to ensure projects are properly planned, staffed, resourced, and executed safely, efficiently, and profitably. This position provides leadership and support to regional operations, field supervision, project management, and estimating while maintaining a strong focus on customer satisfaction, operational efficiency, and company growth.

Responsibilities:

* **Scheduling & Resource Allocation:** Oversee companywide project scheduling, prioritize work, and allocate crews, equipment, and resources across all markets to maximize efficiency and utilization.
* **Crew Staffing & Workforce Planning:** Coordinate staffing needs, crew assignments, and workforce development to ensure adequate personnel are available to meet project demands.
* **Project Management & Estimating:** Provide oversight and direction to project management and estimating teams, ensuring accurate project handoffs, effective execution, cost control, and profitability.
* **Regional & Field Support:** Support regional managers and field supervisors with operational decisions, project execution, personnel management, and day-to-day challenges.
* **Material Forecasting & Planning:** Coordinate material forecasts, procurement planning, and delivery schedules to ensure timely availability of stabilization materials while minimizing downtime and costs.
* **Jobsite Troubleshooting:** Provide hands-on support in resolving field challenges involving soil conditions, equipment, production, scheduling, and constructability.
* **Engineering & Value Engineering:** Collaborate with engineers, customers, and project teams to identify value engineering (VE) opportunities and cost-effective stabilization solutions.
* **Preconstruction Planning:** Lead coordination between estimating, project management, and field operations to ensure project scope, schedules, manpower, equipment, materials, and potential risks are addressed before mobilization.
* **Customer Relationships:** Maintain a customer-focused approach, support key customer relationships, resolve project concerns, and ensure commitments are met.
* **Operational & Financial Performance:** Monitor project profitability, productivity, equipment utilization, scheduling performance, and operational costs while driving continuous improvement.
* **Safety & Quality:** Promote consistent safety standards, quality workmanship, accountability, and best operational practices across all markets.

Qualifications:

* **Qualifications**

 + 10+ years of experience in soil stabilization, heavy civil construction, earthwork, or related specialty contracting.
 + Proven experience managing multiple projects, crews, and geographic markets.
 + Strong understanding of construction operations, scheduling, equipment utilization, project management, and estimating.
 + Knowledge of soil stabilization methods, materials, equipment, and field applications preferred.
 + Strong leadership, communication, organizational, and problem-solving skills.
 + Ability to balance strategic planning with hands-on field support and operational decision-making.
 + Willingness to travel between markets and project locations as needed.

 **Key Performance Expectations**

 + Maximize crew and equipment utilization across all markets.
 + Maintain effective scheduling and project readiness.
 + Improve project productivity and profitability.
 + Minimize operational downtime and resource conflicts.
 + Strengthen regional and field leadership performance.
 + Deliver consistent quality and customer satisfaction.
 + Support sustainable company growth through efficient operations.

People Promise:

**Our People Promise**

**Make your next move an expert one.**

At Colliers it’s not our success that sets us apart, it’s how we achieve it. Our people are passionate, take ownership and always do what’s right for our clients, people and communities.

**Why Colliers?**

Our enterprising environment needs your expertise to facilitate Colliers’ continued growth as an industry leader. Our nimble, decentralized culture can provide you with a wealth of opportunities to learn about our business and quickly gain experience to accelerate your career.

***\*\*this is an on-site opportunity based out of our Atlanta, GA office\* \****

 

**About the role**

The Director, Brokerage Operations will lead the effective and consistent delivery of operational excellence across the office and serve as the local integrator for the business. The role will lead through influence across a matrixed organization, coordinating local, regional and national resources to achieve business objectives around producers and the point of sale, regardless of reporting structure. The Director will oversee the day-to-day operating and administrative requirements for local business lines while maintaining clear accountability for outcomes.

As a key member of the local leadership team, the Director will organize enablement around winning business, recruiting, retention and producer effectiveness. The role will use the broader Colliers platform aggressively where it can deliver work better or more efficiently, while ensuring strong local execution and continuous improvement in service delivery.

 

**In this position, you will..**

* Lead and manage operations support employees across departments, ensuring service excellence, efficient delivery, clear accountability and continuous improvement in all service areas.
* Lead adoption of enterprise technology platforms, automation initiatives and process improvements to drive scalability, producer efficiency and operational effectiveness.
* Bring strong operating and financial rigor to the business in collaboration with the local Managing Director, including P&L management, budgeting, forecasting, capital planning, financial analysis and resource allocation. Partner with Finance on transactional processes without making transactional Finance the center of the role.
* Serve as a strategic business partner to the Managing Director, supporting office revenue growth through producer recruiting, onboarding and integration, retention, producer productivity and pursuit conversion. Coordinate supporting resources and deliverables, including pitch books, recruiting materials and meeting preparation.
* Maintain an effective audit process to ensure local revenue recognition and other key controls are followed in accordance with company and GAAP guidelines.

* Partner with the local Managing Director on annual business planning, growth and market expansion, workforce planning and execution of strategic priorities, translating priorities into recommendations and action while ensuring corporate policies and procedures are followed.

* Operate proactively and decisively across a matrix, resolving issues at the appropriate level and making difficult calls rather than routinely pushing decisions upward.
* Integrate local, regional and national resources, including Client Services, analysts, People Services, Marketing, Research, IT, Operations and Finance, around producers and the point of sale. Leverage the broader Colliers platform for better, more efficient delivery while retaining clear local accountability.

**About the Team**

Dow Jones Energy is a leading global energy intelligence business providing trusted price reporting from our specialist Price Reporting Agency (PRA) OPIS, Chemical Market Analytics (CMA) and McCloskey, proprietary data, market intelligence, news and research to help customers navigate increasingly interconnected energy markets. Through our specialist businesses, Dow Jones Energy makes it easier to discover and access trusted expertise spanning oil and gas, chemicals, refined fuels, coal, electric vehicle infrastructure and renewables. Our specialist businesses combine rigorous pricing methodologies with world-class human judgment to deliver the trusted intelligence and specialist insight customers need to make confident decisions.

**About the Role**

The Director of Business Optimization & Operational Excellence will play a pivotal role in transforming commercial operations into a highly efficient, value-impacting engine. Reporting directly to the VP of Operational Excellence, this role is tasked with managing the Business Optimization team driving the end-to-end Customer Journey process improvement, strengthening commercial and commercial operations execution, and enabling sustainable business growth. In addition, implement systematic collection of VOC across customer facing functions for actionable insights.The successful candidate will leverage Lean management frameworks, process mapping methodologies, automation technologies, and advanced Salesforce CRM optimization to eliminate friction across commercial workflows. Furthermore, this role will champion cross-functional alignment and operational efficiency across critical commercial partnering functions, including Sales Excellence, Customer Service, Sales Coordination, RevOps, Marketing, Billing and Legal teams.

**You Will**

The Director of Quality Improvement operates under the leadership and direction of the Chief Medical Officer (CMO) and Chief Operating Officer (COO). The CMO maintains direct clinical oversight of clinical quality improvement activities and regulatory quality programs. The Director of Quality Improvement provides organization-wide leadership for EVCHC's quality improvement program. The Director establishes the quality strategy in partnership with executive, clinical, operational and compliance leaders; converts organizational goals and regulatory requirements into measurable work plans; and leads improvement efforts that strengthen patient outcomes, safety, access, equity and care experience. The Director is accountable for reliable quality data, required clinical quality reporting, continuous improvement methods, Patient Centered Medical Home recognition, and the performance of the Quality Improvement Department.

 

***MAJOR POSITION RESPONSIBILITIES AND FUNCTIONS:***

**Quality Strategy and Governance**

* Lead the development, implementation and annual evaluation of EVCHC's organization-wide Quality Improvement and Quality Assurance Plan in alignment with the strategic plan, clinical standards and applicable Health Center Program requirements.

* Establish annual quality priorities, measures, targets, owners and timelines with executive and clinical leadership. Monitor progress and recommend corrective action when performance does not meet established goals.

* Lead or support the Quality Improvement Committee and related workgroups. Prepare agendas, dashboards, meeting materials, decisions and follow-up reports for executive leadership and the Board of Directors, as requested.

* Advise executive leaders on emerging quality risks, performance trends, resource needs and opportunities to improve care delivery across sites and service lines.

* Promote a culture of continuous improvement, accountability, patient safety and learning throughout the organization.

**Department Leadership**

* Direct the work of the Quality Improvement Department, including recruitment, onboarding, supervision, coaching, performance evaluation, workload assignment and staff development.

* Develop departmental goals, staffing plans, procedures and budgets that support timely completion of quality priorities and reporting obligations.

* Set clear expectations for the accuracy, timeliness and usability of analyses, audits, reports and improvement support provided by the department.

* Build effective working relationships with clinical care teams, Operations, Information Technology, Compliance, Human Resources, Finance, Behavioral Health, Dental and other departments involved in quality outcomes.

**Quality Measurement and Reporting**

* Oversee the collection, validation, analysis and submission of clinical quality measures and required reports, including Uniform Data System measures, population health platforms transition and readiness, HEDIS and payer measures, grant measures and internal quality indicators.

* Develop and maintain executive, provider, site and service-line dashboards that show current performance, trends, disparities, targets and improvement actions.

* Track provider and care-team performance, identify variation and care gaps, and provide leaders with actionable information while maintaining appropriate confidentiality and data-use standards.

* Establish data-validation controls and documentation so that quality reports can be reconciled to source systems and used as an organization-wide source of truth. Partnering with Director of Data and IT operations for oversight on data governance committee.

* Present quality findings in clear written and verbal reports to the Board, executive leadership, managers, providers, staff, health plans and external reviewers, as appropriate.

Shield AI is a venture-backed defense-tech company with the mission of protecting service members and civilians with intelligent systems. Its products include Hivemind autonomy software, V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft, and Aechelon simulation and synthetic reality technologies. With offices and facilities across the U.S., Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific, Shield AI’s technology actively supports operations worldwide. For more information, visit www.shield.ai https://shield.ai/. Follow Shield AI on LinkedIn https://www.linkedin.com/company/shield-ai, X https://x.com/shieldaitech, Instagram https://www.instagram.com/shield_ai, and YouTube https://www.youtube.com/@Shield_AI. 

 


JOB DESCRIPTION:

The Compensation Director, Aircraft Engineering and Manufacturing, serves as the strategic compensation leader for the Aircraft division, providing enterprise-level oversight for compensation programs supporting manufacturing, production, operations, supply chain, logistics, customer success, and skilled trades. This role defines compensation strategy for large, complex employee populations while ensuring programs are competitive, scalable, compliant, and aligned with business objectives. 

As the organization's subject matter expert for manufacturing and operations compensation, the Director partners closely with business leaders, Px Business Partners, Finance, and Legal to design compensation programs that enable business growth, talent attraction, workforce scalability, and operational excellence. 

The ideal candidate brings deep expertise in manufacturing compensation strategy, non-exempt workforce design, market intelligence, and executive consulting, with a demonstrated ability to influence enterprise decisions and build compensation frameworks that support rapidly growing operations. 

What you'll do:

Compensation Strategy & Enterprise Leadership 

 - Develop and lead the compensation strategy supporting Aircraft manufacturing, production, operations, supply chain, logistics, customer success, and skilled trades populations.  

 - Serve as the SME on manufacturing and operations compensation, shaping long-term compensation philosophy and governance.  

 - Partner with business leadership to align compensation strategy with business growth, workforce planning, organizational design, and operational priorities.  

 - Drive compensation initiatives supporting facility expansions, new business models, geographic growth, and workforce transformation.
