**Company Summary:**

We are a fast-growing, innovative company that is revolutionizing global health. At Vireo and pH-D you will be on the ground-floor of an exciting fast-growing company that focuses on its core values and is passionate about improving the lives of people and pets by delivering premium, health products through world-class research innovation and manufacturing.

**Position Summary:**

The Plant Manager has full operational accountability for the chemical manufacturing facility at Vireo Resources in Plattsmouth, Nebraska. This leader owns facility performance from raw material readiness through batch execution, finished product handoff, and shipment readiness. The role delivers safe, consistent, efficient, and cost-effective batches that meet approved specifications and production commitments, with direct accountability for people, production, manufacturing cost, equipment reliability, and continuous improvement.

**Role and Responsibilities:**

* **Operational Leadership:** Lead facility operations across all shifts, aligning production schedules, staffing, materials, and equipment availability to meet demand. Manage budgets and drive improvements in productivity, cost, quality, and delivery.
* **Process and Technical Leadership:** Apply chemistry and engineering expertise to improve manufacturing processes and resolve recurring issues. Partner with cross-functional teams to lead startups, establish operating standards, and ensure consistent execution of approved procedures.
* **Safety, Quality, and Compliance:** Ensure operations meet safety, environmental, and quality requirements. Oversee chemical handling, process safety, and emergency readiness, and lead corrective actions with EHS and Quality while preserving Quality’s independent product release authority.
* **People Leadership:** Hire, coach, and develop facility teams, ensuring effective shift coverage and employee competency. Establish clear expectations and reinforce accountability, collaboration, and Vireo’s core values.
* **Strategic Planning and Performance:** Develop capacity and improvement plans that support company growth. Execute approved capital projects and communicate operational results, financial performance, risks, and recovery plans to leadership.

**Requirements:**

* Bachelor’s degree or above in Chemistry, Chemical Engineering, Process Engineering, or a related field.
* 8+ years in chemical manufacturing, including 3+ years leading plant operations. Experience must include people, production, and budget accountability.
* Proven batch manufacturing leadership with measurable improvements in yield, cycle time, quality, output, and cost.
* Strong budgeting, cost analysis, capacity planning, and KPI management skills.
* Strong knowledge of chemical processes, reaction engineering, utilities, and automated controls. Translate technical issues into practical decisions and communicate clearly.
* Ability to lead a 24/7 operation and respond to urgent operating issues.
* Proven ability to develop teams, set expectations, and hold employees accountable.
* Strong troubleshooting and root cause analysis skills. Demonstrated success preventing recurring failures.
* Knowledge of Lean, Six Sigma, or similar improvement methods. Certification preferred.
* Commitment to safety, environmental stewardship, quality, and compliance. Plant startup, commissioning, or expansion experience preferred.
* Travel up to 10%

**Physical Demands / Work Environment:**

* Ability to stand, walk, climb stairs, and perform essential plant duties, with or without reasonable accommodation up to 10 hours.
* Must be able to occasionally lift up to 50 pounds
* Ability to work around chemicals, heat, noise, and equipment using required safeguards and PPE.
* Availability for extended hours or weekends during startup, outages, emergencies, and critical operations.

**Compensation + Benefits:**

* Base salary + bonus based on company and personal performance
* Medical, Denta

The Market Director, Facility Operations provides strategic and operational leadership for facility operations across the East Pierce Market within MultiCare Health System, including hospitals, ambulatory sites, urgent care centers, clinics, medical office buildings, and other healthcare facilities. 
 
This role is accountable for market-level facility operations, plant operations, building systems, property management, regulatory compliance, infrastructure reliability, and facility-related operational planning.
 
 
The Market Director serves as the primary operational partner between East Pierce Market leadership and system Facilities Management & Operations Support Services (FMOSS), Planning, Design & Construction, Real Estate, and other enterprise support teams.

Shield AI is a venture-backed defense-tech company with the mission of protecting service members and civilians with intelligent systems. Its products include Hivemind autonomy software, V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft, and Aechelon simulation and synthetic reality technologies. With offices and facilities across the U.S., Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific, Shield AI’s technology actively supports operations worldwide. For more information, visit www.shield.ai https://shield.ai/. Follow Shield AI on LinkedIn https://www.linkedin.com/company/shield-ai, X https://x.com/shieldaitech, Instagram https://www.instagram.com/shield_ai, and YouTube https://www.youtube.com/@Shield_AI. 

 


JOB DESCRIPTION:

Shield AI is seeking a Strategy & Operations Director to help define enterprise strategy and ensure its operational execution. This role offers immersive exposure to the company’s most critical decisions — spanning aircraft systems, AI software (Hivemind), autonomy hardware, and international growth.

As a core member of the Strategy & Operations team, you’ll apply structured problem‑solving, financial rigor, and operational discipline to turn strategic priorities into actionable, measurable outcomes. The role combines high‑performance expectations with a strong learning and development environment — ideal for professionals seeking to grow into future strategy, operations, or general management leaders.

What you'll do:

 - Enterprise Strategy Development:
 
 - Lead the multi‑year strategic planning and annual operating strategy cycles.
 
 - Evaluate portfolio tradeoffs across platforms, software, hardware, and emerging growth vectors.
 
 - Conduct market sizing, competitive analysis, and scenario modeling across U.S. and allied defense markets.
 
 Capital Allocation & Business Case Rigor:
 
 - Build financial models and analytic frameworks for investment decisions (new platforms, manufacturing, international expansion).
 
 - Assess TAM, margin structure, capital intensity, payback, and risk‑adjusted returns.
 
 - Contribute to the development of enterprise‑wide capital allocation frameworks and governance processes.
 
 Operationalization of Strategy:
 
 - Translate strategic priorities into cross‑functional execution plans with defined KPIs and milestones.
 
 - Track and report on progress through structured operating cadences (monthly and quarterly performance reviews).
 
 - Identify bottlenecks, analyze root causes, and recommend actionable solutions to sustain execution velocity.

Required qualifications:

 - Min 12+ years of experience with Bachelors, 8+ with Masters, and 5+ with PhD.

 - Min 4+ years’ experience in a top-tier strategy consulting, corporate strategy or other high‑rigor roles.

 - Strong analytical and conceptual problem‑solving abilities.

 - Demonstrated ability to structure ambiguous problems and drive insight through analysis.

 - Financial modeling and analytical capability (unit economics, forecasting, scenario analysis).

 - Experience or strong interest in complex, technical, or regulated industries (aerospace, defense, AI, or advanced manufacturing preferred).

 - Ability to work collaboratively across teams and influence senior stakeholders.

 - U.S. citizenship required (ability to obtain and maintain a security clearance).

**Senior Director, Manufacturing Operations**

*Own the supply chain and CMC project engine behind Nurix's clinical programs and commercial readiness. In this multifaceted role, you will select and manage CMOs, keep clinical supply flowing to trial sites around the world, and drive cross-functional CMC plans from early development toward commercialization, in a small, entrepreneurial environment with broad responsibilities.*

 

**Position Description**

The position is a multifaceted role supporting several areas within the Technical Operations group, including supply chain management, CMC project management, and clinical labeling and distribution. The ideal candidate will be highly motivated and self-directed, with experience and interest in working in a small, entrepreneurial environment with broad responsibilities and opportunities.

 

**The Opportunity**

* Lead the effort to identify, select, and manage Contract Manufacturing Organizations (CMOs) for the development and cGMP manufacture of raw materials, RSMs, and DS in support of ongoing clinical programs and commercial products (with finance and commercial teams)
* Manage global supply chains and logistics in support of demand for clinical studies and commercial products
* Working in conjunction with technical teams, provide vendor management support in all logistics and operations to ensure on-time delivery of materials
* Coordinate the design and execution of cross-functional CMC project plans and budgeting for early clinical development through commercial readiness
* Maintain frequent communication with cross-functional CMC project team members and key internal stakeholders so that all parties are aware of current project status, issues, contingencies, milestones, and budgets
* Proactively identify the CMC critical path, risks, and impediments to successful development, and drive the identification and development of solutions to mitigate these risks
* Serve as primary clinical supply chain contact, working collaboratively with internal and external partners
* Manage clinical supply planning and forecasting for study protocols and develop packaging/labeling and global distribution strategies
* Monitor IXRS portal processes, including high and low enrolling site settings, drug acknowledgement, depot and site supply levels, and IMP status of released lots or expired drug
* Coordinate the preparation and/or review of CMC sections of INDs, CTAs, NDAs, MAAs, and other regulatory submissions to ensure timely distribution of clinical trial materials
* Coordinate the process validation programs to support commercialization
* Initiate and manage high-value intercontinental, cross-border, and domestic shipments
* Coordinate the preparation, review, editing, and approval of cGMP batch records and CMC regulatory and Quality documents
* Coordinate the preparation of technical reports, publications, and oral presentations

 

**What You'll Bring**

* BS with 15+ years' experience; degree in Pharmaceutical Chemistry, Organic Chemistry, Pharmaceutics, Pharmaceutical Science, or a related scientific discipline
* At least 10 years of relevant experience in a pharmaceutical or biotechnology CMC/cGMP environment
* Excellent project management skills and the ability to work cross-functionally to develop and execute project plans
* Experience managing US and international CRO/CMOs for the manufacture of raw materials, RSMs, and cGMP DS and DP for programs in development
* Experience with clinical supply chain, including forecasting supply needs
* Experience with cGMP manufacturing and IND, CTA, and NDA filings; thorough knowledge of relevant FDA and EMEA regulations
* Experience in supply chain management, and experience establishing pharmaceutical supply chain systems and networks
* Able to identify and resolve critical issues
* Sufficient technical background and experience to work closely with other technical functional areas
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills, and e

Karman Space & Defense is a leader in the rapid design, development, and production of critical, next-generation system solutions that align with the U.S. Department of War and its allies' core mission priorities, and meet the accelerating demand for access to space. Building on nearly 50 years of success, we deliver Payload & Protection Systems, Aero/Hydrodynamic Interstage Systems, and Propulsion & Launch Systems to more than 80 prime contractors supporting over 130 space and defense programs.

The Director of Manufacturing Automation leads the enterprise roadmap for practical, scalable automation across Karman manufacturing facilities. This leader partners with site operations, manufacturing engineering, quality, IT, and finance to identify high-return opportunities, pilot and deploy solutions, and sustain measurable improvements in safety, throughput, labor productivity, and quality. The role balances strategic technology selection with hands-on shop-floor execution and is accountable for standardizing successful solutions across multiple locations. 
 
**Responsibilities** 

* Develops and owns the enterprise manufacturing automation strategy, investment roadmap, and prioritized project portfolio.
* Identifies and quantifies automation opportunities through site assessments, capacity analysis, labor studies, and business cases with measurable returns.
* Leads implementation of robotics, CNC tending, automated inspection, material handling, and other fit-for-purpose production technologies.
* Partners with IT and cybersecurity teams on machine connectivity, industrial controls, data integrity, and secure integration with enterprise systems.
* Establishes standards for automation architecture, equipment acceptance, safety validation, commissioning, documentation, and maintainability.
* Coordinates cross-functional project teams and vendors to deliver automation installations within approved cost, schedule, and performance targets.
* Works with Quality and Engineering to validate automated processes, product conformity, and controlled changes in regulated manufacturing environments.
* Develops site technical capabilities through training, change management, and sustainable maintenance and support plans.
* Tracks automation performance using utilization, overall equipment effectiveness, cycle time, yield, labor hours, and realized financial benefits.
* Provides executive reporting on project status, risks, capital needs, and enterprise replication opportunities.

**Required Qualifications** 

* Bachelor's degree in engineering, manufacturing, automation, or a related technical discipline, or equivalent relevant experience.
* 10+ years of manufacturing engineering, industrial automation, or related technical experience, including 5+ years leading complex projects or teams.
* Demonstrated deployment of industrial automation solutions in discrete manufacturing environments.
* Experience developing capital business cases, managing vendors, and delivering projects against financial and operational targets.
* Working knowledge of industrial controls, robotics, machine interfaces, functional safety, and production data systems.
* Ability to lead across multiple sites and influence stakeholders without direct reporting authority.

**Preferred Qualifications** 

* Aerospace and defense manufacturing experience, including AS9100-controlled production.
* Experience with CNC automation, automated inspection, machine monitoring, and ERP/MES integration.
* Lean Six Sigma certification or demonstrated continuous improvement leadership.
* Advanced engineering degree or professional automation certification.

**Special Mentions** 

* Travel of up to 50% is required to Karman manufacturing facilities, suppliers, and project locations, based on business needs.
* Future relocation to a designated Karman location may be required based on evolving business needs. Any relocation expectations will be discussed with the employee in advance.
* Ability

**About the University**

 

Established in 1965, Metropolitan State University ( MSU Denver ) was founded to serve students who were underrepresented in higher education whose life paths and experiences did not fit the traditional mold. Sixty years later, the University continues to serve over 16,000 of Colorado’s extraordinary and diverse students, providing them with the foundation on which to build their unique aspirations. As the third largest public institution of higher education in Colorado, MSU Denver is a model university for today’s college students.

Proud of its federal designation as a Hispanic-Serving Institution that also offers graduate programs (gHSI) and the only Seal of Excelencia certified institution in Colorado, the University serves the most diverse undergraduate student population in the state, as well as the most first-generation students. Through affordable, flexible, and holistic education, MSU Denver helps students build essential skills grounded in a multicultural and global perspective that lead to undergraduate and graduate degrees, and career and life success.

 

At MSU Denver, we are committed to our CADRE values: Community, Access, Diversity, Respect, and Excellence. We strive to create a supportive and inclusive environment where all community members are valued and belong. Our dedication to breaking down barriers to education, fostering open dialogue, and promoting world-class scholarship ensures that we provide exceptional services and innovative learning opportunities for our students, faculty, and staff.

 

**Position Summary**

 

MSU Denver seeks a Director to lead the Advanced Manufacturing Sciences Institute ( AMSI ) and advance its development into a sustainable, impactful program. The Director manages all AMSI activities including the Industry 4.0 Center of Excellence which serves Colorado manufacturers through technology demonstrations, training, micro-credentials, and sponsored partnerships. The Director is the primary liaison and point of contact for all industry partners. The Director develops and maintains the Advanced Manufacturing Sciences academic programs in collaboration with various academic departments.

The Director builds integrated pathways for both degree-seeking students and non-degree learners. These pathways connect credentials, work-based learning, undergraduate and graduate programs, and lifelong learning. The Director also makes AMSI a hub for interdisciplinary collaboration within CACED and across the University. Through AMSI, the Director connects academic programs, faculty, students, industry partners, and community organizations around shared learning, applied research, workforce development, and emerging opportunities.

A high priority for the Director is to develop a long-term model that allows AMSI to sustain and grow its programs and activities beyond short-term or one-time funding. The incoming Director will build appropriate revenue-generating activities to support students, programs, equipment, and future growth.

 

**Responsibilities**

 

Institute Strategy

* Set and carry out AMSI’s mission, vision, and annual plan consistent with the strategy, budgets, goals, and policies of CACED and the University.
* Advance industry-relevant technologies, practices, and partnerships that prepare students to contribute from their first day on the job and that address manufacturing workforce gaps.
Maintain an active Advisory Board and keep it informed through an outcomes dashboard that tracks sponsors, student credit hours, enrollments, non-degree learners served, placements, revenue by source, and other appropriate data. 

Institute Sustainability

* Develop a long-term sustainability model and a multi-year business plan that sets out AMSI’s costs, funding sources, and revenue sources; update the plan each year.
* Build a diversified funding base that combines earned r

Shield AI is a venture-backed defense-tech company with the mission of protecting service members and civilians with intelligent systems. Its products include Hivemind autonomy software, V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft, and Aechelon simulation and synthetic reality technologies. With offices and facilities across the U.S., Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific, Shield AI’s technology actively supports operations worldwide. For more information, visit www.shield.ai https://shield.ai/. Follow Shield AI on LinkedIn https://www.linkedin.com/company/shield-ai, X https://x.com/shieldaitech, Instagram https://www.instagram.com/shield_ai, and YouTube https://www.youtube.com/@Shield_AI. 

 


JOB DESCRIPTION:

Shield AI is seeking a highly driven Sr. Manager Materials Planning & Logistics to lead supply planning, material readiness, production planning, and logistics execution for next-generation autonomous aircraft development programs and a new greenfield manufacturing facility. This leadership role is accountable for establishing the people, processes, systems, and infrastructure required to support rapid product development, new product introduction, and the transition to scalable rate production. 

The ideal candidate combines strong operational leadership with hands-on execution, thrives in fast-paced environments, and has experience building manufacturing and supply chain capabilities from the ground up. You will work cross-functionally with Engineering, Program Management, Quality, Procurement, and Operations teams.  

What you'll do:

Development Program Materials Planning  

 - Own the materials planning, production control, inventory, warehousing, and logistics strategy. 

 - Partner with Engineering, Program Management, and Procurement to develop and maintain accurate build plans that are aligned with program milestones.   

 - Define and monitor key performance indicators for schedule attainment, material availability, shortage reduction, inventory health, work-order execution, and planning accuracy. 

 - Identify long-lead material risks and implement mitigation strategies to protect schedule. 

 - Oversee the development and execution of material recovery plans. 

 - Drive engineering change management processes to support rapid development and ECO implementation.   

 - Develop planning models that support rapid prototyping, design iteration, and low-rate initial production activities.   

 - Support executive-level program and operations reviews by clearly communicating material status, risks, business impacts, and required decisions. 

Greenfield Facility Build & Operational Readiness  

 - Lead planning and logistics readiness activities for a new manufacturing facility.   

 - Design and implement warehouse, stockroom, and material flow processes from receiving through point-of-use consumption.   

 - Establish inventory control procedures, material storage standards, and transaction discipline.   

 - Partner with Manufacturing Engineering and Facilities teams to optimize material movement and operational efficiency.   

Team Leadership  

 - Create a culture focused on accountability, operational excellence, continuous improvement, and mission execution.   

 - Establish standard work and training programs.   

 - Drive cross-functional collaboration to solve complex challenges.   

Required qualifications:

 - Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain, Operations, Engineering, Business, or related field.   

 - 7+ years of experience in materials planning, inventory management, or supply chain operations.   

 - Experience supporting complex hardware development programs in aerospace, defense, automotive, robotics, or advanced manufacturing environments.   

 - Demonstrated experience implementing or scaling material planning and inventory management processes.

The Regional Director of Operations is responsible for providing operational leadership, client partnership support, and strategic oversight for multiple senior living dining and hospitality accounts within an assigned region. This position partners closely with community leadership teams, culinary operations, resident experience teams, and corporate leadership to ensure operational excellence, financial performance, hospitality culture, regulatory compliance, and elevated resident satisfaction across all assigned communities.

Position Type and Expected Hours of Work

This is an exempt salaried position, with expected hours to include: days, evenings, weekends, and holidays.

Essential Functions and Duties

Operational Leadership

* Provide leadership and operational oversight for multiple senior living dining and hospitality accounts
* Support and mentor Directors of Dining Services, Executive Chefs, Resident Experience leaders, and community management teams
* Ensure operational consistency, hospitality standards, and service excellence throughout all assigned communities
* Conduct regular operational visits, audits, and performance reviews

Client & Resident Relationships

* Build and maintain strong relationships with client leadership teams, residents, families, and operational partners
* Ensure resident satisfaction initiatives and hospitality-focused service culture remain a top operational priority
* Participate in client meetings, operational reviews, and strategic planning discussions
* Address operational concerns and support service recovery initiatives when needed

Financial Management

* Manage regional financial performance including:

* labor management,
* food cost controls,
* budgeting,
* forecasting,
* and overall account profitability

* Analyze financial reports and operational metrics to identify opportunities for improvement
* Support implementation of operational efficiencies and cost-control initiatives

Culinary & Hospitality Excellence

* Support culinary innovation, menu development, dining presentation, and hospitality-driven service initiatives
* Ensure dining environments reflect company hospitality standards and resident experience expectations
* Promote elevated dining experiences throughout all communities

Associate Leadership & Development

* Recruit, coach, mentor, and develop operational leadership teams
* Support associate engagement, retention, succession planning, and performance management initiatives
* Foster a positive, professional, and accountability-driven culture throughout the region
* Assist with onboarding and transition support for new business and leadership changes

Compliance & Quality Assurance

* Ensure compliance with all federal, state, local, and company regulations and standards
* Support sanitation, food safety, healthcare compliance, and regulatory audit readiness
* Conduct operational assessments and quality assurance reviews
* Ensure corrective action plans are implemented and maintained when necessary

Travel

This role will be 80-100% travel. Travel will be by car and/or plane and will include overnight travel.

General Responsibility as Required for Position

The Regional Director of Operations serves as the primary operational leader supporting community-level Directors, Executive Chefs, and management teams while helping drive consistency, service excellence, associate engagement, and overall client satisfaction throughout the region. This role requires strong leadership presence, hospitality mindse, financial acumen, and the ability to build strong operational partnerships within senior living environments

We’re looking for talented professionals to join us in bringing smart money management and payment solutions to everyone’s fingertips.

This position is classified as structured hybrid, with an expectation of three (3) days per week working in the office and flexibility to work remotely on the remaining days. On-site expectations may evolve over time to support business needs, with clear communication provided in advance.

 > > > > > > > > > >

**JOB DESCRIPTION**

**Position Summary**

The Director, Customer Support is a strategic leader responsible for overseeing Customer Support Learning & Development, Quality Assurance, Customer Experience Insights, and Root Cause Management across all customer contact channels. This role drives continuous improvement by ensuring frontline teams, business partners, and vendors have the knowledge, tools, coaching, and quality programs necessary to deliver exceptional customer experiences.

**What Does a Director, Customer Support Do?**

Leads the strategy and execution of Learning & Development, Quality Assurance, Customer Experience Insights, and Root Cause Analysis programs across customer support operations.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Set the vision and strategy for Customer Support programs.
* Lead Learning & Development programs including onboarding, leadership development, and frontline capability building including program enhancements to processes, policies and procedures.
* Oversee quality assurance programs across voice, chat, email, social media, disputes, complaints, and escalations. This also includes oversight and management of the Coaching portal
* Oversight and execution of the root cause analysis program resulting in identification of initiatives to eliminate recurring customer issues and/or improve the overall customers experience
* Serve as the voice of the customer by translating feedback into actionable business improvements.
* Partner with Product, Technology, Compliance, Risk, and Operations leaders to improve customer outcomes.
* Lead managers and teams responsible for QA, L&D, knowledge management, and customer insights.
* Establish KPIs and reporting frameworks to measure effectiveness and drive continuous improvement.

**Success Measures**

* CSAT
* NPS
* Quality Assurance Scores
* Complaint Reduction
* Learning Effectiveness
* Root Cause Resolution
* First Contact Resolution

**Required Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience.
* 10+ years of leadership experience in customer support, quality, learning & development, or operational.
* 5+ years leading managers and cross-functional teams.
* Experience building scalable QA and L&D programs.
* Strong analytical and stakeholder management skills.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Financial services, fintech, banking, or payments experience.
* Experience managing BPO/vendor relationships.
* Lean, Six Sigma, Quality Management, or Organizational Development certifications.

**Leadership Competencies**

* Strategic Leadership
* Customer Centricity
* People Development
* Operational Excellence
* Cross-Functional Influence
* Innovation & Problem Solving
* Execution & Accountability

**POSITION TYPE**

Regular

**PAY RANGE**

The targeted full-time base salary for this position is $127,000 to $200,200 per year. The final compensation will be determined by a number of factors such as qualifications, expertise, and the candidate’s geographical location.

**PLANT OPERATIONS CAREERS**

Plant Manager

Lead a healthcare laundry plant.

**Where** [City, ST]

**Reports to** General Manager / Regional Vice President

As Plant Manager, you'll lead the full plant (production, maintenance, quality, and logistics) with accountability for safety, budget, and the healthcare customers who depend on clean, safe linen every day.

Why you'll like it here

**Own the plant**

Daily operations, people, budget, and results.

**Lean in action**

Drive improvement with Lean Manufacturing and Six Sigma.

**Lead leaders**

Develop supervisors, maintenance staff, and production Associates.

**Healthcare standards**

Run an operation held to OSHA and HLAC requirements.

What you'll own

* Lead and manage the Safety & Health Program within the production environment.
* Lead, motivate, and develop a team of supervisors, maintenance staff, and production associates.
* Oversee daily plant operations, including production scheduling, labor forecasting, staffing, and workflow optimization.
* Drive process improvements using Lean Manufacturing and Six Sigma methodologies.
* Manage plant budget, including labor, maintenance, and operational expenses.
* Oversee inventory management to ensure consistent material supply and stock levels.

What you need

* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Manufacturing, or Business Administration required.
* 5–7 years of leadership experience in a manufacturing or industrial environment.
* Strong end-to-end understanding of plant operations, including safety, quality, maintenance, and compliance.
* Proven experience managing P&L, budgeting, payroll, and cost controls.
* Strong problem-solving, analytical, and strategic thinking skills.
* Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Excel, PowerPoint, Word) and ERP systems.
* Excellent leadership, communication, and organizational skills.

**Physical requirements**

* Ability to stand, walk, and move throughout a manufacturing facility for extended periods.
* Ability to occasionally lift up-to fifty (50) pounds.
* Comfortable working in a plant/production environment.
* Ability to push and pull carts of linen regularly.
* Ability to use required personal protective equipment (PPE), including safety glasses, hearing protection, and work boots.

**Bonus points**

* Experience with Lean Manufacturing and/or Six Sigma methodologies preferred.
* PMP (Project Management Professional) certification.
* Willing to relocate- GOE flexibility.
* Prior military leadership experience (e.g., Sergeant or above) a plus.
* Familiarity with ISO 14001 / ISO 9001 and GMP standards.
* Experience with manufacturing systems and reporting tools

**We'll teach you:** Our plant network, operating standards, and the support of a national organization.

How we work

Every ImageFIRST Associate lives our four Core Values. These are our required competencies.

**Be Respectful**

Value all we come in contact with.

**Be Remarkable**

Create a positive moment with every interaction.

**Be Safe**

Keep ourselves and those around us safe.

**Be Honest**

Be guided by truthfulness in all we do.

Great work gets noticed

**Everyday recognition**

Coworkers nominate each other for going above and beyond, and those nominations go up in the office for everyone to see.

**All Stars & Council of Excellence**

Each year, Associates who live our values are nominated as All-Stars and earn a certificate and a cash award. Top winners join the Council of Excellence with an additional reward.

Benefits

Weekly pay

Medical, Dental, Vision

Pet, Legal, and Hospital Indemnity Insurance

401(k) with company match

Paid Time Off package

Paid Parental Leave

Tuition Reimbursement

Referral Program

Great company culture

Collaborative team environment

 

**MILITARY & VETERANS**

Served? Your skills fit here.

Officers and senior NCOs who led maintenance, logistics, or production operations: command a plant. Whether you're transitioning out, serving in the Guard or Reserve, or a veteran, we want

Are you interested in working for a company that fosters growth opportunities, community involvement and a team-oriented atmosphere? ClarkDietrich fosters a work-life balance and offers competitive compensation and benefits. Join a team that is STRONGER THAN STEEL℠, by applying to become a Plant Manager at our **Riverside** location.

**SUMMARY**

The **Plant Manager** is responsible for the day-to-day operations of the entire manufacturing facility to include safety, quality, efficiencies, and meeting customer expectations. This includes driving strategic plans that ensure that production goals are met in the safest and most cost-effective manner, while delivering expected financial results.

**ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES**

* Direct and manage plant operations for production, maintenance, quality, and shipping and receiving.
* Coordinate plant activities through planning with departmental supervisors/managers to ensure that all manufacturing objectives are accomplished in a timely and cost-effective manner.
* Oversee all aspects of the day-to-day plant operations, including production, maintenance, and logistics.
* Develop, monitor and control plant budget, through active planning and understanding of P&L to ensure financial targets are met.
* Implements cost effective systems of control over capital, operating expenditures, manpower, wages, and salaries.
* Leads the effort and drives Lean Manufacturing tools and techniques fostering continuous improvement within the facility. Acts in a proactive fashion regarding problem resolution.
* Maintains existing plant facilities and equipment; replace or adjust plant facilities and equipment when necessary. Investigate and recommend new equipment or process improvements.
* Actively participated with Regional Sales Management to develop and manage the Regional Operating Unit into a team-oriented environment.
* Establish and monitor overall plant performance for production and quality standards.
* Controls and minimizes labor overtime, premium freight, and repair expenses.
* Provides leadership and training to accomplish the company goals and objectives.
* Incorporates shop floor organization and plant cleanliness among plant personnel.
* Schedules and conducts plant communication which focus on key operative measurements, safety topics and .
* Onsite contact for government agencies, landlords and various other vendors

**SAFETY**

* Strives to improve the plant's safety accident record year after year in creating a positive safety culture for all employees. Conducts safety walks of the facility on a weekly basis.

* Monitors the activities of all employees and provides feedback and discipline to promote a safe workplace.
* Oversee the development and organization of all safety related documentation.
* Ensures and develops all required safety related training and promotes programs to lead safe behaviors.
* Audits equipment and the shop floor for safety related improvements.

**SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES**

* Supervise plant staff and ensure employee safety.
* Mentor staff to create a productive and positive work environment.
* Accountable to Establish strong relationships that foster engaging collaborative influence.

Requirements:

**QUALIFICATIONS**

* Mechanically Inclined.
* Problem Solver.
* Team Oriented.

**EDUCATION AND/OR EXPERIENCE**

* Bachelor's degree in related field or five years plant/general management experience in a manufacturing environment, strongly preferred.
* Working knowledge of budgets and financial statements.
* Background with manufacturing methods, process improvement programs and procedures required.
* Basic computer experience with Microsoft Word and Excel
* The military equivalent will be recognized in lieu of education and/or experience.

**MATHEMATICAL SKILLS**

* Basic mathematical skills, addition, subtraction, multiplication and converting fractions into decimals.
* Ability to read a tape measure, micrometer, and caliper accurately.

**About Luminary Hospice:**
---------------------------

At Luminary Hospice, we are a mission-driven organization that empowers our team members to shape our culture in order to allow them to provide the highest quality support to patients and families throughout their entire end-of-life journey.

Our mission is to deliver personalized care that radiates compassion and preserves dignity for all that we are honored to serve on their end-of-life journey. We are centered on caring for the whole person – with expert medical care, pain management as well as emotional and spiritual support along with resources, information, and emotional support for families and caregivers.

### **About the role:**

The Director of Quality is responsible for leading, designing, and continuously improving the organization's Quality Assurance and Performance Improvement (QAPI) program. This role ensures compliance with all federal, state, and accrediting body requirements while driving a culture of safety, accountability, and high-quality patient care. The Director of Quality partners closely with clinical, operational, and executive leadership to translate quality data into meaningful improvements that enhance patient outcomes, regulatory readiness, and organizational performance.

This leader serves as the organization's subject-matter expert on quality, survey preparedness, and performance improvement, balancing regulatory rigor with practical, frontline-focused solutions.

**Job Responsibilities**

**Quality & Performance Improvement**

* Lead and oversee the organization's QAPI program, ensuring alignment with CMS Conditions of Participation, state regulations, and accreditation standards.

* Develop, implement, and monitor performance improvement initiatives based on data trends, adverse events, and regulatory requirements.

* Analyze quality metrics, patient outcomes, and incident reports to identify risks, root causes, and opportunities for improvement.

* Ensure corrective action plans are developed, implemented, and sustained across departments and markets. (Let's discuss with Nicole)

* Lead mock surveys, tracer activities, and ongoing readiness assessments to ensure continuous compliance.

* Coordinate survey responses, plans of correction, and follow-up activities in partnership with agency leadership.

* Stay current on regulatory changes and proactively educate leaders on impact and expectations.

**Patient Safety & Risk Management**

* Oversee patient safety initiatives, including incident reporting, investigations, and follow-up actions.

* Lead root cause analyses (RCAs) and failure mode assessments as needed.

* Partner with clinical leadership to reduce risk, prevent harm, and improve safety outcomes for patients and staff.

**Data, Reporting & Insights**

* Develop and maintain quality dashboards and reports for executive leadership, agency leaders, and governing bodies.

* Translate complex quality and compliance data into clear, actionable insights.

* Ensure accurate and timely reporting of required quality measures and outcomes.

**Leadership, Education & Collaboration**

* Partner with Executive Directors, Clinical Leaders, and Medical Directors to embed quality expectations into daily operations.

* Support a culture of transparency, continuous learning, and accountability.

* Participate in leadership meetings and provide strategic guidance on quality-related decisions.

Plans, manages and executes the QMS Integration Project Plan (IPP) to update, harmonize and transition the acquired site’s QMS to ZB Global Quality requirements and applicable regulations; to remediate and transfer the site’s QMS and medical device product quality documentation and records from legacy systems into ZB global enterprise IT applications; and to ensure the site obtains and/or maintains certifications and establishment registration.

Partners cross-functionally with Quality, Regulatory, R&D, Operations, Supplier Quality, Post-Market Surveillance, Servicing, IT, the Integration Management Office (IMO) and acquired-site leadership to complete integration on schedule and within budget while maintaining continuous regulatory compliance, product supply and in-process regulatory submissions.

* Leads cross-functional, multi-workstream QMS integration projects for newly acquired medical device businesses, from post-close planning through harmonization, documentation transfer, verification of effectiveness and integration closure.

Shield AI is a venture-backed defense-tech company with the mission of protecting service members and civilians with intelligent systems. Its products include Hivemind autonomy software, V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft, and Aechelon simulation and synthetic reality technologies. With offices and facilities across the U.S., Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific, Shield AI’s technology actively supports operations worldwide. For more information, visit www.shield.ai https://shield.ai/. Follow Shield AI on LinkedIn https://www.linkedin.com/company/shield-ai, X https://x.com/shieldaitech, Instagram https://www.instagram.com/shield_ai, and YouTube https://www.youtube.com/@Shield_AI. 

 


ABOUT SHIELD AI:

Shield AI is a venture-backed defense technology company with the mission of protecting service members and civilians with intelligent systems. Our products include Hivemind autonomy software, V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft, and Aechelon simulation and synthetic reality technologies. 


JOB DESCRIPTION:

We’re looking for a hands-on manufacturing leader to take X-BAT from early prototype builds through production launch and into rate production. 

You will lead prototype build execution and the manufacturing setup of our new Seattle-area facility, X-Forge 3. You’ll build the production team, establish the factory’s operating system and deliver the readiness needed to scale aircraft production safely, reliably and efficiently. 

This role carries accountability across the full journey: turning lessons from development builds into a repeatable production system, then leading that operation against safety, quality, delivery and cost commitments. You’ll work closely with Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Quality, Supply Chain and Program Management to make that happen. 

What you'll do:

 - Lead prototype builds and new product introduction 
 
 - Own the day-to-day execution of X-BAT prototype and development aircraft builds, including assembly, integration, rework and build support for testing. 
 
 - Partner with Program Management to establish achievable build schedules, resource plans and milestones, making constraints and trade-offs visible early. 
 
 - Work with Engineering and Manufacturing Engineering through build-test-learn cycles, ensuring build issues are captured, resolved and reflected in future designs and production processes. 
 
 - Plan and execute pre-series builds to prove tooling, work instructions, material flow, process controls and workforce readiness before production ramp. 
 
 - Maintain configuration discipline and aircraft traceability throughout development builds in partnership with Engineering and Quality. 
 
 Establish the Seattle production operation 
 
 - Lead manufacturing setup and operational readiness for X-Forge 3, working with Facilities and Manufacturing Engineering on factory layout, equipment installation, commissioning and production flow. 
 
 - Recruit, develop and lead the production organization, building capable frontline leadership and a skilled aircraft assembly team. 
 
 - Own production staffing, training and capacity plans, aligning investment and workforce growth with program demand. 
 
 - Drive launch readiness across people, tooling, materials, processes and quality, with clear owners and closure plans for gaps. 
 
 - Lead the transition from prototype operations into Seattle production, ensuring build knowledge and lessons learned transfer with the work. 
 
 Deliver and scale aircraft production 
 
 - Own production execution against safety, quality, delivery and cost targets as X-BAT moves through initial production and into sustained rate. 
 
 - Establish daily operating routines, visual management and escalation processes that surface problems early and drive timely resolution. 
 
 - Improve throughput, labor productivity, first-pass quality and schedule adherence through practical Lean methods and structured problem-solving. 
 
 - Partner with Supply Chain and Planning to align

Karman Space & Defense is a leader in the rapid design, development, and production of critical, next-generation system solutions that align with the U.S. Department of War and its allies' core mission priorities, and meet the accelerating demand for access to space. Building on nearly 50 years of success, we deliver Payload & Protection Systems, Aero/Hydrodynamic Interstage Systems, and Propulsion & Launch Systems to more than 80 prime contractors supporting over 130 space and defense programs.

This role is part of our Space and Launch business, which has contributed to the nation's space programs for decades by delivering complete solutions from concept to flight. We enable successful space operations with mission-critical technology supporting every step from first launch to final landing, including launch vehicle subsystems, propulsion systems, aerodynamic and interstage systems, and payload protection and deployment. Our high-performance solutions are engineered to operate in the most extreme environments and meet precise mission requirements.

The Director of Production Planning leads the enterprise production planning and scheduling operating system across Karman's manufacturing operations. In this role, you will transform customer demand and Sales, Inventory and Operations Planning (SIOP) outputs into executable production plans, capacity strategies, and recovery actions that support on-time delivery and predictable execution while providing visibility into risks, constraints, and opportunities across the manufacturing network.

**Responsibilities**

* Leads production planning, master scheduling, and finite-capacity planning across Karman manufacturing sites and value streams.
* Translates customer demand, backlog, and Sales, Inventory and Operations Planning (SIOP) outputs into achievable production schedules with clear priorities, constraints, and recovery plans.
* Establishes planning standards and key performance indicators (KPIs) for schedule adherence, on-time delivery, past-due backlog, work-in-process (WIP) aging, capacity utilization, and plan attainment.
* Partners with Operations and Manufacturing Engineering to align labor, equipment, tooling, and process capacity with production requirements.
* Coordinates with Supply Chain to identify material shortages, supplier constraints, and outside-processing risks before they affect production performance.
* Leads schedule recovery and re-baselining efforts when demand, material availability, quality issues, or capacity changes create delivery risk.
* Ensures enterprise resource planning (ERP), material requirements planning (MRP), and planning data are accurate, timely, and aligned with approved operating plans.
* Develops planners and schedulers while building a high-accountability planning organization.
* Provides executive visibility into delivery risk, capacity gaps, staffing needs, and critical decisions required to protect customer commitments.
* Improves end-to-end SIOP, planning, scheduling, and production-control processes.

**Required Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain, Operations, Engineering, Business, or a related field.
* 10+ years of production planning, master scheduling, operations planning, or supply chain experience in a manufacturing environment.
* 5+ years of leadership experience managing planning, scheduling, or production-control teams.
* Demonstrated experience with ERP, MRP, master production schedules, capacity planning, and material requirements planning.
* Strong analytical skills and experience leading cross-functional delivery-recovery plans.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience in aerospace, defense, space, or other highly regulated manufacturing environments.
* Experience with SIOP, Sales and Operations Planning (S&OP), Power BI, or advanced manufacturing analytics.
* Knowledge of AS9100 and configuration-controlled manufacturing environments.

**Leading the Change in Youth Development**

At Boys & Girls Clubs of King County, we are taking youth programming to a new level. We are one of the largest Club organizations in the country, and we pride ourselves on always doing what is best for youth. As leaders in youth development, we provide a safe place for kids and teens during critical out-of-school time that is affordable for all families. Our Clubs offer life-changing programs and services to youth in greater Seattle. We prioritize a youth-centric Club experience through culturally relevant, inclusive, and diverse programming delivered by individuals committed to serving youth.

Inframark's Operations and Maintenance team is an award-winning team that delivers cutting-edge water, wastewater, and public works services to municipalities, utility districts, and industries. We are dedicated to supporting our employees as well as protecting the environment and the communities we serve. You would be empowered to thrive in a dynamic, supportive, and innovative environment. Take the next step in your career and join us at Inframark. Apply today!
 
Why Work for Inframark?
 
 
Our dedication to sustainability and community impact drives us to ensure clean, safe water for future generations. Whether you're at the start of your career or looking for advancement, Inframark offers purpose-driven work and opportunities for growth. We offer an attractive salary package, including a generous benefits package with health, dental, and life insurance, 401(k) plan, paid time off, sick leave, holidays, and wellness plan.
 
 
Water Operations Supervisor
 
Jasper GA
 
Are you an experienced water professional ready to take the next step in leadership? We are seeking a Water Operations Supervisor to oversee the day-to-day operation, maintenance, and regulatory compliance of our water treatment and distribution systems. In this role, you'll lead a skilled team, ensure safe and efficient plant operations, and play a critical role in delivering high-quality drinking water to the communities we serve.
 
This is an excellent opportunity for a licensed water treatment professional who thrives in a hands-on leadership role and is passionate about operational excellence, team development, and public service.
 
What You'll Do
 
 
**As the Water Operations Supervisor, you will:** 

* Lead the continuous operation of water treatment plants, wells, standpipes, distribution systems, and related infrastructure.
* Supervise and support operations staff, ensuring work is completed safely, efficiently, and in compliance with all regulatory requirements.
* Monitor plant performance and operational processes, making adjustments as needed to maintain system reliability and water quality.
* Prepare and review internal, regulatory, and client reports.
* Verify staff compliance with operational procedures, maintenance programs, laboratory protocols, QA/QC standards, and safety requirements.
* Conduct regular meetings with department leaders to review performance metrics, operational goals, and continuous improvement opportunities.
* Assist in establishing facility objectives, operational strategies, and workforce planning initiatives.
* Respond effectively to emergency situations and implement corrective actions when necessary.
* Champion a strong safety culture by overseeing and enforcing company safety programs and standards.
* Participate in hiring, interviewing, onboarding, coaching, performance evaluations, and disciplinary processes.
* Develop and approve staff schedules to ensure adequate operational coverage.
* Support budgeting, planning, and administrative functions.
* Serve as acting Project Manager when needed.
* Build positive relationships with customers, clients, municipal officials, and community stakeholders.

Required Qualifications
 

* High school diploma or GED required.

* Valid driver's license with an acceptable driving record.

Overview:

We are seeking a dynamic and experienced Director of Quality and Accreditation to lead our facility’s efforts in ensuring the highest standards of patient care and safety. This leadership role is responsible for overseeing regulatory compliance, quality assurance programs, and continuous improvement initiatives across all clinical and operational areas. The Director will guide the development and implementation of quality protocols, manage accreditation processes, and lead the Quality Assurance and Process Improvement (QAPI) program. The ideal candidate will be a proactive, strategic thinker with a strong commitment to achieving excellence in care delivery and regulatory readiness.

**PURPOSE STATEMENT:**

The Director of Quality and Accreditation is responsible for ensuring patient safety and superior quality of care as measured by survey readiness, treatment program fidelity, and compliance with state and federal laws and regulations and accreditation standards. As such, the Director is responsible for leading and overseeing all aspects of policy development; comprehensive implementation of Acadia’s prescribed clinical protocols, operational quality oversight standards, and programmatic expectations; critical incident reporting; regulatory engagement, including development and submission of plans of correction; certification achievement and maintenance; oversight of the quality assurance and process improvement (QAPI) program; and on-going regulatory readiness strategies at the facility. Through routine physical presence in patient care areas, data analysis and documentation monitoring, and intentional sharing of deep subject-matter expertise, the Director will ensure a proactive, multidisciplinary focus on quality and excellence within the facility.

Responsibilities:

**ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:**

* Lead and monitor day-to-day regulatory readiness, patient safety, and service excellence across the facility.
* QAPI program oversight and management – follow and develop processes for identification, collection, and analysis of quality performance data.
 + Utilize collected data regarding the outcome of activities for delivering continuously improving services.
 + Conduct annual preparation and evaluation of the facility QAPI Program.
 + Complete process improvement projects and incorporate the results into patient care improvements.
 + Submit quality scorecard data to Acadia corporate office as requested.
 + Coordinate the abstraction of clinical data according to Joint Commission specifications and data entry via vendor database for Inpatient Psychiatric Core Measures (ex. national quality measures such as HBIPS).
 + Identify key aspects of care relevant indicators and evaluation of data using formal and informal feedback from consumers of services and other collateral sources is aggregated and used to improve management strategies and service delivery practices.
 + Lead/coordinate data collection and analysis from all departments within the facility.
 + Prepare and present program data trends and action plans to the monthly Quality Council and quarterly to the Medical Executive Committee and the Governing Board.
* Regulatory preparedness – implement sustainable survey preparation and ongoing monitoring processes, including facility-wide auditing and early-issue identification, to maximize achievement of zero- or standard-level survey outcomes.
 + Facility-wide support – collaborate with other departments to sustainably implement best-practices in regulatory/accreditation compliance as evidenced by measurable results with regard to survey outcomes, patient safety metrics, patient experience results, HBIPS, etc.
 + Develop and maintain proficiency in regulatory planning strategy for all standards for all relevant regulatory and accrediting bodies at the local, state, and federal level.
 + Develop and maintain proficiency in the functionality and auditing within electronic platforms such as electronic patient observatio

**Foundation Risk Partners****, one of the fastest growing insurance brokerage and consulting firms in the US, is adding a** ***Director of Operations-Insurance*** **to their team in** ***Lakeland, FL.***

**Job Summary:**

The Commercial Lines Operations Leader is responsible for overseeing the operational effectiveness, service delivery, and strategic execution of commercial lines insurance processes. This role ensures alignment with business goals, regulatory compliance, and a high standard of customer and broker satisfaction. The leader will drive continuous improvement, operational efficiency, and team performance across underwriting support, policy servicing, and client onboarding.

**Essential Functions:**

* **Operational Leadership:** 
 Lead day-to-day operations for commercial lines, ensuring timely and accurate processing of policies, endorsements, renewals, and cancellations.
* **Process Optimization:** 
 Identify and implement process improvements to enhance efficiency, accuracy, and scalability of operations.
* **Team Management:** 
 Manage and develop a high-performing team, including training, performance management, and career development.
* **Cross-Functional Collaboration:** 
 Partner with underwriting, claims, IT, compliance, and sales teams to ensure seamless service delivery and operational alignment.
* **Technology & Automation:** 
 Leverage technology and automation tools to streamline workflows and reduce manual tasks.
* **Compliance & Risk Management:** 
 Ensure adherence to regulatory requirements, internal controls, and company policies.
* **Reporting & Analytics:** 
 Monitor KPIs, service levels, and operational metrics to drive data-informed decisions and continuous improvement.
* **Customer Experience:** 
 Champion a customer-first mindset, ensuring high service standards for brokers, agents, and policyholders.

**Competencies & Qualifications:**

* 7+ years of experience in insurance operations
* Proven leadership experience managing teams and driving operational excellence
* Strong knowledge of insurance products, systems, and regulatory environment
* Excellent communication, analytical, and problem-solving skills
* Change management and process improvement expertise

**Education & Experience:**

* Bachelor's degree in Business, Insurance, or related field preferred
* Experience with insurance platforms (e.g. Applied Epic)
 

**Disclaimer:**

While this job description is intended to be an accurate reflection of the job requirements, management reserves the right to modify, add, or remove duties from particular jobs and to assign other duties as necessary.

**Equal Employment Opportunity (EEO):**

FRP provides equal employment opportunity to qualified persons regardless of race, color, sex, religion, national origin, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability, veteran status, or any other classifications protected by law.

**Benefits:**

FRP offers a comprehensive range of health-related benefit options including medical, vision, and dental. We offer a 401(k) with company match, company paid life insurance, STD, LTD and a generous PTO policy starting at 18 days per year plus 10 paid holidays & 2 floating holidays!

You'll lead and develop regional operations teams, oversee service installations and maintenance, and drive the performance, safety, and efficiency of our field operations.

This is an opportunity to make a meaningful impact as Lumos continues to expand, combining strategic leadership with hands-on operational expertise to strengthen service delivery, improve processes, and build high-performing teams that support our customers and continued growth.

This is a remote position supporting Service Operations across the Midwest region, with a preference for candidates located within a Lumos market in **Ohio, Indiana, or Kentucky**. Regional travel is required.

**Why Lumos:**

Lumos is transforming the future of connectivity by building one of the nation's fastest-growing 100% Fiber Optic networks. Through T-Fiber, our joint venture with T-Mobile, we're working toward a shared goal of connecting 12 to 15 million homes by 2030 while expanding access to reliable, high-speed internet in the communities we serve.

Here, you'll find more than a job, you'll have the opportunity to make an impact, take ownership of your work, and help shape how we grow. We move quickly, collaborate across teams, and believe the best ideas come from people who are curious, solutions-oriented, and ready to build what's next.

**What You'll Do:**

* Lead, coach, and develop regional Service Operations managers and teams, fostering accountability, collaboration, and a strong customer-first culture.
* Oversee service installations, maintenance, and field operations across assigned markets, ensuring consistent quality, safety, and operational performance.
* Establish and monitor KPIs, SLAs, and customer experience metrics to drive efficiency, service reliability, and continuous improvement.
* Develop and execute operational strategies that support market expansion, service delivery objectives, and long-term business growth.
* Manage department budgets, resources, and operational projects to ensure effective planning, execution, and cost management.
* Oversee vendor and contractor performance, including negotiations, service expectations, and accountability for operational results.
* Serve as a key escalation point for complex customer and operational challenges, driving timely resolution and improvements to the customer experience.
* Partner across Network Operations, Engineering, Construction, Customer Care, and other teams to improve workflows, strengthen service delivery, and support business objectives.
* Establish and maintain operational policies, procedures, and safety standards while identifying opportunities to improve processes and scale operations.

**What You'll Bring:**

* 7+ years of experience in telecommunications service operations, field operations, or a related area.
* Proven experience leading geographically dispersed teams, developing managers, and driving operational performance across multiple markets.
* Strong understanding of telecommunications service installation, maintenance, network operations, and customer service delivery.
* Experience managing operational budgets, vendor relationships, contractor performance, and service-level agreements.
* Ability to analyze KPIs, operational performance, and customer satisfaction metrics to identify trends and drive improvements.
* Strong leadership, communication, problem-solving, and decision-making skills, with the ability to manage competing priorities.
* Proficiency with Microsoft Office and operational software platforms, with the ability to adapt to new systems and technologies.
* A proactive, solutions-oriented approach with the ability to work independently and lead effectively in a fast-paced environment.

**What Makes You a Great Fit:**

* High school diploma or equivalent.
* Bachelor's

record.ROLE_TEXT:
ShipMonk isn't just a 3PL — we're the tech-powered growth partner for ecommerce brands, running 12+ owned fulfillment centers across the US, Canada, the UK, and Europe so our merchants can stress less and grow more.

We are seeking a hands-on Senior Manager to join our Strategy & Operations team and drive the analysis and execution behind initiatives that improve how ShipMonk works across departments. Reporting to our Senior Director of Strategy and Operations, you will turn ambiguous problems into clear analysis, recommendations, and results, and keep leadership aligned through operating reviews and KPI reporting. 
 
What you'll do: 
 
Drive Cross-Department Initiatives

* Own workstreams within major initiatives that improve processes across departments, from mapping how work flows today to tracking results after launch.
* Size opportunities, define requirements, and help teams adopt new processes and tools.
* Lead on-site discovery with frontline teams to understand how work really gets done.

Drive Continuous Improvement

* Find recurring friction in the data and on the floor, and size and prioritize the biggest opportunities.
* Measure results in quality, speed, and the employee and merchant experience, not just cost.

Run Business Operations

* Run operating reviews, KPI reporting, and initiative tracking for senior leadership.
* Prepare clear decision materials, follow up on commitments, and surface risks early.
* Help teams strengthen governance practices that fit how they work.

Analyze and Build

* Analyze productivity, capacity, cost to serve, and profitability, and build models that quantify trade-offs and turn decisions into action.
* Build dashboards, tools, and workflows hands-on with AI tools such as Claude.

What you'll need:

* Bachelor's degree in engineering, business, economics, supply chain, or a related field
* 1–3 years of experience in business analysis, strategy, operations, or management consulting
* Strong analytical and financial modeling skills in Excel or Google Sheets; SQL or BI experience strongly preferred
* A structured, KPI-driven approach to solving ambiguous, cross-functional problems
* Experience with reporting, KPI tracking, or operating reviews is a plus
* Experience building with AI tools such as Claude to speed up analysis and reporting
* Comfort spending time on the warehouse floor and working directly with operating teams
* Exposure to fulfillment, distribution, or manufacturing operations; continuous improvement or Lean experience is a plus
* Clear written and verbal communication, with the ability to influence without direct authority
* Ability to travel 25–35%, with more time on-site during discovery and rollouts

**About ShipMonk**

ShipMonk isn't just a 3PL; we're a **growth partner for merchants**. We provide cutting-edge technology and a network of owned and operated fulfillment centers that empower high-growth ecommerce and DTC brands to stress less and grow more. With over 2,500 employees across five countries, we're on a mission to revolutionize fulfillment by providing everything from the fastest click-to-delivery and real-time inventory to custom solutions—all with a **merchant**-**first** mindset.

**Why ShipMonk?**

We believe in building for the long term, and our success is powered by five key differentiators that help us become true partners to our merchants.

**Confidential Search: ESL Processing Manager – Dairy Manufacturing** 
**Location:** Greater Philadelphia, PA Area 
**Industry:** Dairy / Food & Beverage Manufacturing 
**Employment Type:** Full-time, Onsite 
**Compensation:** Competitive Base + Bonus + Full Benefits 
**Confidential Role – Qualified candidates only will be contacted directly**

### **Position Summary**

A well-established dairy manufacturer in the Philadelphia region is conducting a confidential search for an experienced **ESL Processing Manager**. This role will oversee operations related to extended shelf life milk and dairy beverage processing, with a strong focus on product quality, plant performance, and regulatory compliance.

The ideal candidate will have direct experience with **HTST, UHT, or ESL pasteurization systems**, a deep understanding of **fluid dairy processing**, and a proven ability to lead production teams in a **fast-paced, SQF-certified environment**.

### **Key Responsibilities**

* Lead daily operations of the ESL processing department, ensuring product quality and production efficiency.
* Manage HTST/UHT equipment, CIP/SIP procedures, and aseptic processing protocols.
* Oversee batch formulation, temperature and flow controls, and compliance with state and federal regulations.
* Coordinate production schedules, sanitation cycles, and preventative maintenance in conjunction with QA and maintenance teams.
* Lead, train, and supervise ESL line operators and processing staff; enforce safety, GMP, and food safety practices.
* Monitor and improve KPIs related to yield, run efficiency, downtime, and loss.
* Collaborate with R&D, Quality Assurance, Packaging, and Distribution teams on process improvement initiatives.

### **Required Qualifications**

* 5+ years of dairy or beverage processing experience, with at least 2 years in an ESL, HTST, or UHT operation.
* Strong understanding of fluid milk or dairy-based beverage production and regulatory compliance (FDA, PMO).
* Supervisory or leadership experience in a food manufacturing plant.
* Familiarity with CIP/SIP systems, flow schematics, and thermal processing validation.
* Bachelor’s degree in Food Science, Dairy Science, Engineering, or a related field preferred.
* Strong communication, problem-solving, and organizational skills.
* Experience working in SQF-certified or similar food safety environments.

### **Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience with aseptic packaging lines or ESL bottled products.
* Pasteurizer or processing certifications (e.g., HACCP, SQF Practitioner).
* Knowledge of automation systems (e.g., PLCs, SCADA) used in fluid processing.

**To Apply Confidentially:** 
Please send your resume and brief cover note to **laws@henpencorp.com** 
Or text **408-755-5423** to express interest.

*Only qualified applicants with relevant dairy or ESL processing experience will be contacte*

**About Achievement First**

Achievement First (AF) is a non-profit 501(c)(3) organization that currently supports 41 public charter schools in New York, Connecticut, and Rhode Island. Consistently rated as one of the top charter school networks in the country for almost 25 years, AF is committed to continuous improvement, programmatic evolution for enhanced student outcomes, and sustainable growth. The majority of AF students are Black and Latinx children from low-income families who will be the first in their families to graduate from college. AF currently employs more than 2,200 staff — 64% of whom identify as Black, Indigenous, and People of Color — who collectively educate nearly 15,000 students in Brooklyn and Queens, NY; New Haven, Bridgeport, and Hartford, CT; and Providence, RI.

The mission of Achievement First is to deliver on the promise of equal educational opportunity for all of America's children. AF knows that every child—regardless of race, zip code, or economic status—deserves access to great schools. At AF, students realize their potential and develop the skills they need to graduate from high school, succeed in college, thrive in a competitive world, and serve as the next generation of leaders in their communities. At AF, students and staff embark on a shared journey to fulfill their incredible potential.

 

*We are looking for a* Managing Director of Academic Program Operations *to join our Academic Strategy & Execution team.*

**Your Impact**

The Managing Director of Academic Program Operations will serve as a senior strategic partner and operations expert working with the Academic Program Team to deliver on the implementation of Achievement First's school model & instructional priorities. This role is ideal for someone who has a deep knowledge of schools both as instructional institutions but also the intersection with funding, finance, operations, and talent practices. The Managing Director of of Academic Program Operations will partner with the Deputy Chief of Academic Strategy & Execution and other senior program leaders to deliver on a cohesive & coherent experience of our school model and support the change management involved in refining our model to align to our aims for our Achievement First graduates anchored in knowledge of self & community, college, career, & life readiness, and purpose & leadership. The Managing Director of Academic Program Operations does not need to be the content expert in any given domain, but should be a fast learner able to bring people together to solve challenges & inspire change, and be able to communicate across a variety of stakeholders including school leaders & school based staff, as well as leaders of functional teams in the organization.

* Managing the implementation of our current school design and instructional priorities

 + Oversee the annual planning, operations actions and execution needed across curriculum, assessment, professional learning operations, school budget development, calendar and the operations behind our instructional priorities needed to deliver our current model and priorities with excellence
 + Partner with Deputy Chiefs of School Design, and senior Academic Program leads to opera

JOB DESCRIPTION:

The Compensation Director, Aircraft Engineering and Manufacturing, serves as the strategic compensation leader for the Aircraft division, providing enterprise-level oversight for compensation programs supporting manufacturing, production, operations, supply chain, logistics, customer success, and skilled trades. This role defines compensation strategy for large, complex employee populations while ensuring programs are competitive, scalable, compliant, and aligned with business objectives. 

As the organization's subject matter expert for manufacturing and operations compensation, the Director partners closely with business leaders, Px Business Partners, Finance, and Legal to design compensation programs that enable business growth, talent attraction, workforce scalability, and operational excellence. 

The ideal candidate brings deep expertise in manufacturing compensation strategy, non-exempt workforce design, market intelligence, and executive consulting, with a demonstrated ability to influence enterprise decisions and build compensation frameworks that support rapidly growing operations. 

What you'll do:

Compensation Strategy & Enterprise Leadership 

 - Develop and lead the compensation strategy supporting Aircraft manufacturing, production, operations, supply chain, logistics, customer success, and skilled trades populations.  

 - Serve as the SME on manufacturing and operations compensation, shaping long-term compensation philosophy and governance.  

 - Partner with business leadership to align compensation strategy with business growth, workforce planning, organizational design, and operational priorities.  

 - Drive compensation initiatives supporting facility expansions, new business models, geographic growth, and workforce transformation.  

Manufacturing & Operations Compensation 

 - Lead the design and evolution of compensation structures supporting large non-exempt employee populations.  

 - Establish wage structures, geographic differentials, shift premium strategies, progression frameworks, and other compensation programs that balance external competitiveness with internal equity.  

 - Oversee market pricing methodologies utilizing Radford, Mercer, WTW, and specialized manufacturing compensation surveys alongside complementary market intelligence.  

 - Develop innovative compensation approaches to attract and retain highly competitive manufacturing, technical, and operational talent. 

Executive Partnership & Business Consulting 

 - Serve as the trusted compensation advisor to Aircraft executives and business leaders.  

 - Consult on organization design, workforce investments, location strategy, and talent acquisition decisions with significant financial and organizational impact in partnership with the Px Business Partner.  

 - Provide strategic guidance on compensation implications of organizational changes, acquisitions, new facilities, and business expansion.  

 - Present compensation recommendations and analyses to executive leadership with clear business rationale and risk assessments.  

Compensation Analytics & Insights 

 - Lead enterprise compensation analyses including market competitiveness, pay equity, workforce cost modeling, and incentive effectiveness.  

 - Translate complex compensation
